categories.name: Narrative scene, gesture & narrated events
categories.desc: Fiction scene beats, character movement and body language, entering/starting, narrated past incidents, emotion and demeanour.

categories.desc: Speech acts: say/said, attribution colons, speaker stance in talk, and questions as discourse objects.

categories.name: Speaker & addressee: I, we, you
categories.desc: Second-person address to the reader or interlocutor, and first-person authorial/inclusive we.

categories.name: Conversation, confrontation & colloquial register
categories.desc: Live exchanges: I/you in dialogue, confrontation, forum asks and thanks, consent between parties, plus casual spoken vocabulary.

categories.name: Minds, perception & persons
categories.desc: Knowing/seeing/remembering, pronoun subjects of mental-state clauses, appraisal and feelings, person nouns, gender and age.

categories.name: Document deixis, self-reference & naming
categories.desc: The text pointing at itself or elsewhere in itself (here/herein, this paper, figures/tables), naming and aboutness.

categories.desc: URLs, see-also links, reference lists, citation strings, paper front matter.

categories.name: Biomedical & life-science papers
categories.desc: Molecular biology, clinical, lab-methods and natural-history prose, from prelude term-piece detectors to coda word-pickers.

categories.name: Math, STEM & academic prose
categories.desc: Math notation, physics/math exposition, and general academic methods and abstract-noun vocabulary.

categories.desc: Bible verses, psalms, hymns, prayers, sermons and theology.

categories.desc: Nineteenth-century books, scanned print, archaic diction, biography and genealogy records.

categories.name: Web, commerce & media genres
categories.desc: Consumer health copy, dating spam, recipes, web-page furniture, film/TV, sports and game descriptions.

categories.name: Contrast & concession
categories.desc: however, though, but, still, yet, and reluctant-compliance turns.

categories.name: Substitution & alternatives
categories.desc: instead/rather, other/another/else, either/or/neither.

categories.name: Cause, inference & sequence connectives
categories.desc: because/due to, therefore/thus/hence, then/thereafter/otherwise.

categories.name: Similarity, comparison & difference
categories.desc: same/similar/like, together/combined, comparatives (more/less/than), difference, between/among.

categories.name: Hedging, stance & epistemic qualification
categories.desc: probably/perhaps/seems, degree and litotes, negation with stance verbs, scope limits, frequency hedges.

categories.name: Restriction, focus & exemplification
categories.desc: only/just/merely/solely, and example-giving (for example, such as).

categories.name: Necessity & sufficiency
categories.desc: need/required, enough/sufficient/adequate.

categories.name: Modals, auxiliaries & copula
categories.desc: would/can/could/will, have/has/had, being/having, -able, and copula-to-predicate writers.

categories.name: Relative, complement & wh-clauses
categories.desc: which/that/where/when/while, complementizer that, interrogative and embedded how/what/whether.

categories.name: Prepositions
categories.desc: with, for, from, into/onto, through/via, and the slots and complements around them.

categories.name: Phrasal particles
categories.desc: out, off, down, back, over, and the verbs that take them.

categories.name: Pronouns, possessives & deixis
categories.desc: Reflexives, possessive determiners, third-person they/them/him, demonstratives and here/there.

categories.name: Negation, polarity & quantifiers
categories.desc: not/nothing, any/anything, each/every, all/whole, one, both/pairs.

categories.name: Calendar, durations & time
categories.desc: years, months, weekdays, dates, durations, until, time as a resource.

categories.name: Temporal order & sequence
categories.desc: before/after/prior, later/subsequently, first/initially, document numbering.

categories.name: Now, change, onset & recurrence
categories.desc: now/currently/recency, future, change and transformation, new, begin/start, already/previously, again/once more.

categories.name: Numbers, quantity & measurement
categories.desc: Small counts, ordinals, spelled-out numbers, large magnitudes, amount/total, size/scale, per-rates.

categories.name: Place & spatial layout
categories.desc: Place nouns and geographic scale, top/bottom/side, right/left, lines and borders.

categories.name: Public affairs, economy & the physical world
categories.desc: Politics and government, institutions and funding, prices and markets, industry, safety, weather and terrain, testing.

categories.name: Single-lemma readout families
categories.desc: Coda clusters that push or block one content word: head, use, set, case, part, point, way, free, end, type/style.

categories.name: Code & software
categories.desc: Source code, developer Q&A, CLI help, and the syntax/markup/identifier tokens inside code.

categories.name: Numeric data & encoded blobs
categories.desc: Digits inside CSV/float/hex dumps, base64 and random strings, ID columns, structured punctuation.

categories.name: Subword & name-fragment detectors
categories.desc: Prelude detectors of word pieces, name fragments, OCR debris and bytes, with no shared meaning.

categories.name: Non-English text
categories.desc: Subword pieces in Finnish, Germanic, Romance, CJK, Korean, Cyrillic and other non-English text.

categories.name: Artefact: shared lens direction
categories.desc: Clusters united only by a Jacobian-lens or steering direction (British vs American spelling, document era, casual vs formal, utilize, etc, 'vast quantity', United States steering) while firing is unrelated.

categories.name: Unassigned / mixed
categories.desc: Grab-bags with no shared firing, output or steering story, and incoherent singletons.

clusters.name: Technical, code and patent text mix
clusters.desc: Grab-bag of neurons whose strongest firings sit inside technical documents: source code, markup, patents, papers, numeric tables. Mostly sub-token or digit positions; outputs are scattered. Pass-2 heavy. No single shared concept.

clusters.name: Academic apparatus and output-word suppressors
clusters.desc: Mixed cluster: some neurons fire in reference lists, peer-review and patent prose; several late coda neurons simply suppress one common noun (job, text, effective). Little shared meaning beyond formal written register.

clusters.name: Prelude mixed bag, British-spelling lens
clusters.desc: Mostly early-layer neurons with diverse firing (code tokens, OCR German, legal prose, news). A recurring output signature is British spellings (favour, programmes, honour) in the Jacobian lens. Otherwise no shared theme.

clusters.name: Place and location output words
clusters.desc: Neurons, mostly late core and coda, whose output direction promotes or suppresses place/location/position nouns (and nearby role, character, local). Firing contexts are generic; the output view carries the story.

clusters.name: URLs, links and citation apparatus
clusters.desc: Pushing these neurons makes the model emit web links and image-host or wiki URL fragments; outputs promote http/wiki/references. Firings lean toward reference sections, DOI lines, see-also pointers. Document apparatus rather than content.

clusters.name: Base64 and encoded-data blobs
clusters.desc: Large cluster spread across all depths whose strongest firings are on characters inside base64 / encoded binary strings (keys, embedded images, certificates). Steering and output views are unrelated to this; the firing view alone carries it.

clusters.name: Finnish and Romance-language fiction
clusters.desc: Two coda neurons firing on sub-word pieces inside non-English narrative prose, chiefly Finnish, with some Italian and French novel text. No steering effect beyond chance; outputs are word fragments.

clusters.name: Comparison and baseline vocabulary
clusters.desc: Mostly pass-2 neurons whose output (esp. Jacobian lens) promotes or suppresses compare / versus / baseline / control words; firings sit in scientific methods and results prose. Output and firing roughly agree; steering mostly weak.

clusters.name: Chemistry patents; coda single-word pickers
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy cluster firing in chemical, materials and patent-claim prose. Each late neuron's output pushes or blocks one word family (product, construction, conduct, preferably, liquid). Firing and output loosely agree on the technical register.

clusters.name: Web front-end code: CSS, HTML, SVG
clusters.desc: Prelude-heavy cluster firing on tokens inside stylesheet, markup and SVG code (flex layout, tooltip classes, utility classes, style attributes, component imports). Firing carries it; a few coda neurons' outputs echo style words (fill, solid, word).

clusters.name: Appraisal, feelings and expectation words
clusters.desc: Neurons whose steering and output push evaluative or mental-state vocabulary: opportunity, feelings, expecting, excellent, doubting, condition. Firings are in informal personal writing, forums and fiction, but loosely tied. Steer and output agree; firing weaker.

clusters.name: Sequence connectives: then, thereafter, otherwise
clusters.desc: Pass-2-heavy cluster whose output direction (esp. Jacobian lens) promotes or blocks sequencing/consequence connectives such as then, thereafter, after, otherwise, thereby. Firings are diffuse across procedures, fiction and forums; output carries the theme.

clusters.name: Demonstrative this, plus coda word-pickers
clusters.desc: Loose cluster: many members fire on or promote the demonstrative this/these (anaphoric reference to the situation at hand), mixed with coda neurons that each push one word (whole, subject, business, sad). Contexts are informal web and forum prose.

clusters.name: Reflexive pronouns and own/self
clusters.desc: Clear family: steering makes the model write myself/itself/themselves, outputs promote or suppress the full reflexive paradigm, and firings land on own, himself, possessives before a reflexive slot. Grammatical self-reference, not meta-commentary. Pass-2 heavy.

clusters.name: British-register lens (whilst, utilise); mixed firing
clusters.desc: Prelude and pass-1 neurons united mainly by a shared Jacobian-lens signature promoting or suppressing British/formal spellings (whilst, utilise, maximise). Firing contexts are unrelated: code, numbers, forum posts, patents. Output carries the grouping.

clusters.name: Second person: addressing you
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to addressing a reader or interlocutor: outputs promote or suppress you/your/yourself, firings sit on second-person forms in reviews, advice copy, forum replies, scripture and screen dialogue. Mostly in both core passes. The addressee axis.

clusters.name: Program code: calls, getters, config values
clusters.desc: Neurons firing inside source code and config files: method calls after a dot, get/read accessors, map over collections, boolean config values, process IDs. Several coda members output one programming word (default, get, yes/true). Firing carries it; output partly agrees.

clusters.name: Health, diet and supplement web copy
clusters.desc: Neurons firing in consumer health writing: weight loss, blood pressure, supplements, skincare, plus much spun SEO spam. Late members output sensory and body words (taste/smell, weight, appealing, active ingredients). Steering and output agree where present.

clusters.name: Old-book narrative prose, word detectors
clusters.desc: Prelude-dominated cluster whose top firings are in nineteenth-century books, sermons and scanned fiction. Many are word detectors (echo, silence, anger, fame, slowly, companion) whose Jacobian lens names the same word; steering is weak. Literary narration register.

clusters.name: Informal Q&A and forum talk, mixed
clusters.desc: Core-layer neurons whose firings fall on function words (you, that, the, but) inside forum answers, help threads and chat. Outputs are scattered; a few coda members push one verb family (speaking, standing, wanting). Discourse texture rather than one concept.

clusters.name: Causal connectives: because, due to
clusters.desc: Pass-2 heavy cluster whose output direction promotes or suppresses causal connectives (because, since, due, owing). Steering sometimes emits reason/due. Firing contexts are generic informal and expository prose, so the output view carries it.

clusters.name: Singleton: with-detector
clusters.desc: One prelude neuron, a near-pure detector of the preposition with in conversational and news prose (top-firing selectivity 1.0). Steering and output show nothing coherent.

clusters.name: Biomedical research prose; coda word-pickers
clusters.desc: Coda-dominated cluster firing in biomedical and life-science papers (physiology, pharmacology, cell biology). Late members each push or block one word family (organs, smooth, mass vs media, pattern, keep, simple). Firing gives the register, output the specifics.

clusters.name: Singleton: digits in CSV ID columns
clusters.desc: One pass-2 neuron firing on trailing digits of ID numbers in CSV-style data rows; negative pole on letters inside place-name lists. Outputs incoherent; firing only.

clusters.name: Contrast connectives: however, though, but
clusters.desc: Strong family: steering makes the model write however/though, outputs promote or suppress however, nevertheless, nonetheless, but, and firings sit at the comma slots where a concessive turn lands. Pass-2 heavy. Sister to the causal and sequence connective clusters.

clusters.name: Mixed late-layer comparison and lexical neurons
clusters.desc: Large heterogeneous cluster. A recurring sub-theme is comparison: neurons firing on comparatives and quantity words before a following than, or writing/suppressing than and related exception words. Others are scattered token or subword detectors.

clusters.name: Mid-word fragments in names and OCR
clusters.desc: Large mixed cluster of subword detectors that fire inside words: pieces of surnames, foreign words, spaced-out or capitalized headings in scanned books, and OCR noise. Coda members output word-continuation suffixes. No semantic theme.

clusters.name: Inline math notation detectors
clusters.desc: Firing-carried cluster of neurons that fire inside mathematical notation: LaTeX delimiters, exponents, fraction numerators, operators, absolute-value bars, matrices and trig functions. Output and steering views are mostly unrelated noise.

clusters.name: Finnish (and other non-English) subword detectors
clusters.desc: Neurons firing on mid-word subword pieces in Finnish text, mostly older Finnish fiction, with a few on Hungarian, Serbo-Croatian or Dutch. Output and steering views are unrelated English vocabulary; the story is in firing.

clusters.name: Selection-marker antibiotic names (singleton)
clusters.desc: Single neuron firing on the first subword of antibiotic or selection-agent names in molecular biology and patent methods text; negative pole on polymer molecular-weight wording. Jacobian lens suppresses biomolecule words.

clusters.name: Necessity and requirement
clusters.desc: Concept cluster about need: neurons that fire where something is required or needed and whose outputs promote necessary, required, needed, requisite or urgent. Steering also surfaces need words. Mostly late core pass 2 and coda.

clusters.name: Mixed identifier and fragment detectors
clusters.desc: No coherent theme. Firing is on scattered subword fragments in code identifiers, foreign names, newsgroup paths and data strings. A shared oddity: many Jacobian lenses favour British-spelled formal verbs (the utilise family), likely a lens artifact rather than meaning.

clusters.name: Document era axis: old vs contemporary
clusters.desc: Neurons whose outputs sit on a time-of-writing axis: mid-20th-century vocabulary on one side, recent-years vocabulary (pandemic, social media, inclusive terms) on the other. Firing is on years, dates and legal case citations. Includes a pass-1/pass-2 pair (36/1098 and 56/1098).

clusters.name: Duration and until (temporal continuation)
clusters.desc: Neurons whose outputs promote until/till/indefinitely/steadily, firing where an ongoing state or process is described (interim phrasing, temporary-state idioms, characters sitting and staring, time-limited offers). The coherent story is the duration output; prelude exemplars are unrelated script/symbol detectors.

clusters.name: Early-layer token and markup detectors
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons (positions 2-17) that detect single tokens or markup: URL path pieces, code braces, markdown heading hashes, subword fragments in names. No shared meaning. Many Jacobian lenses again lean to British-spelled verbs, likely a lens artifact.

clusters.name: Preposition and complement slots
clusters.desc: Neurons firing on prepositions (with, for, of, on, by) and on verbs that take a prepositional complement, often anticipating the next content word. Outputs vary by neuron (exception, instruction, immediate/frequent, characterized). Syntax-level, loosely coherent.

clusters.name: Math-paper symbols and variables
clusters.desc: Large firing-carried cluster, concentrated in prelude positions 5-8: neurons that fire on single-letter variables, Greek letters, subscripts, equation numbers and operators in research-paper math (analysis, PDEs, Hilbert spaces). Output and steering views are unrelated.

clusters.name: Coda next-word predictors after with
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons whose output promotes or suppresses one specific upcoming word family (respect, partner, blood, spray, frozen, exercise, bound), often firing on a preposition like with that sets up that word. Lexical prediction, not a shared concept.

clusters.name: Head word family (head, heading, chief)
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to the word head and its relatives: head as body part, leader (chief, principal), heading/title in documents, or hardware ports and pins. Mostly visible in steering and lens; firing is scattered across code and document headers.

clusters.name: Block endings: end, closing braces
clusters.desc: Neurons around ending: firing on block closers in code (end keywords, closing braces, line breaks before end) and outputs promoting or suppressing end/start/beginning. Partial agreement; several members are generic code-syntax detectors.

clusters.name: Hedging, degree and concession
clusters.desc: Discourse cluster of qualification: neurons firing on weak-evidence and degree words (tendency, faint, smaller-degree phrasing, probably) and on concessive/causal connectives; outputs lean to but, somewhat, albeit, maybe, partially, or suppress yet/but. Academic and scientific register dominates.

clusters.name: Code-context subword detectors (early layers)
clusters.desc: Very large cluster dominated by position 2: near-deterministic detectors of one subword inside code, paths, identifiers and tech-forum text (a capital letter, cap, anches, md, racts). Some late members have output tied to software words (server, backup).

clusters.name: Prelude subword and name fragments
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons (positions 9-14) firing on fragments of names, foreign words, dictionary entries and numbers. No shared meaning. Many Jacobian lenses point at the behaviour/behavioural spelling family, which looks like a shared lens direction rather than content.

clusters.name: Past-tense events and narrated incidents
clusters.desc: Late-layer neurons tied to reported past events: outputs promote was/had/formerly over now/currently, or write event words (accident, discovery, pause, intervening). Firing sits in historical prose, news of incidents and narrated scenes, including interjection speech tags.

clusters.name: Politics, government and news media
clusters.desc: Coherent coda-heavy cluster on public affairs: elections and candidates, presidents and ministries, parties and congresses, press and media, elites and commerce, regions and capitals. Steering, lens and firing largely agree; news register.

clusters.name: Entering and starting motion (singleton)
clusters.desc: Single neuron firing on verbs of entering, coming along or starting up in narrative scenes; its output suppresses arrival/entrance words. Negative pole on command-line argument syntax in code.

clusters.name: Code punctuation and line breaks
clusters.desc: Neurons firing on structural punctuation in source code: line breaks after closing brackets, commas in object literals, loop-condition colons, PowerShell brackets. Several have negative poles on the word and. Late members carry single-word outputs (dry, building, button, enter).

clusters.name: Aboutness: about, regarding, concerning
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to topic-marking: firing on the word about (after information, or asking what makes something appealing) and outputs promoting about/regarding/concerning/pertaining or topic nouns (matters, issues). Text-about-text flavour; several members are unrelated.

clusters.name: Future time and anticipation
clusters.desc: Concept cluster around the future: neurons firing on next time, anytime soon, near future, rising newcomers, thanking beforehand, and outputs promoting future/upcoming/next/forthcoming (or suppressing them). Mostly core pass 2.

clusters.name: Inference connectives: therefore, thus, hence
clusters.desc: Discourse cluster of consequence and inference: outputs promote therefore/thus/hence/consequently/accordingly, firing where a conclusion is drawn (unsurprising outcomes, logical entailment, consequence markers) or where a statement is about to be quoted. Prelude members are unrelated token detectors.

clusters.name: Coda neurons steering against 'over'
clusters.desc: Shared thread is output-side: many coda units suppress 'over' and its variants at readout; firing is scattered subword or preposition hits with no common scene. Prelude members are unrelated subword detectors.

clusters.name: Mixed prelude/core-1 noise detectors
clusters.desc: No coherent theme. Members fire on stray spaces, URL fragments, code punctuation, subwords, and gibberish strings; steering and lens outputs are unrelated vocabulary. Looks like a catch-all of low-level token detectors in prelude and early core.

clusters.name: Either/or: alternatives and binaries
clusters.desc: Strong shared output story: many core-pass-2 and coda units promote or suppress 'either', 'whichever', 'whether', 'neither'. Firing lands on binary oppositions, disjunctions, and conditional dependence. A choice-between-alternatives family.

clusters.name: 'With' complements and reception verbs
clusters.desc: Loose cluster around the preposition 'with' and verbs taking it: met with, credited with, rest with, consulted. Some output units are clean lexical pairs (with/without, greater, short, discharge). Firing carries most; coherence is moderate.

clusters.name: Digits in legal citations; number words
clusters.desc: Firing is dominated by digits and spaces inside case-law reporter citations and dates; output views promote or suppress spelled number words and ordinals. Contains a pass-1/pass-2 pair (module 676 at positions 34 and 54).

clusters.name: Prelude subword detectors, official documents
clusters.desc: Mostly early-prelude token detectors (single subwords, spaces, labels) whose contexts are drawn from government, regulatory, and legal documents. Theme is the document register more than any concept; output views unrelated.

clusters.name: Suppressors of 'utilize' (jlens)
clusters.desc: Shared output signature: the Jacobian lens of most members pushes down 'utilize/utilizing'. Firing is heterogeneous (whether, itself, views, series labels). Likely a register axis against corporate/jargon wording rather than a firing concept.

clusters.name: Mixed: '-ing' forms and reactions
clusters.desc: Weak cluster. Several units involve '-ing' suffixes or emotional reaction words (surprise, disturbing, moving, fitting in), but firing contexts are diverse and output views do not converge.

clusters.name: Output family around 'use'
clusters.desc: Many coda and pass-2 units promote or suppress 'use/usage/uses' at readout; one pairs with 'choice/choose'. Firing is scattered (code identifiers, foreign subwords, passive constructions). Output-carried token family.

clusters.name: Mixed physical and evaluative words
clusters.desc: No single theme. Members span plausibility, accident/incident reporting, hands and protective wear, tools held in hand, healing and rebuilding. Views rarely agree beyond single units.

clusters.name: Old literary/formal prose, degree words
clusters.desc: Leans toward 19th-century and formal prose: idioms of speech qualification, superlatives and degree (utmost, foremost, extreme), hastily, reformation. Exemplars are mixed; firing carries a register rather than one concept.

clusters.name: Digits inside long numeric data
clusters.desc: Clear formatting cluster: core neurons fire on digits, decimal points, and commas inside CSV rows, float arrays, SVG path coordinates, and tables. Steering and output views are unrelated to this.

clusters.name: Second-person output axis
clusters.desc: Shared output signal: many members push 'you/your/yourself' up or down via the Jacobian lens or logit lens. Firing is scattered (code, citations, headers). Relevant to addressee modeling but only output-carried.

clusters.name: Singleton: no coherent profile
clusters.desc: Single neuron with scattered firing (comma after place name, code identifier, subword) and a jlens that suppresses 'utilize'. Unlabelable as a theme.

clusters.name: Biography, genealogy, and historical records
clusters.desc: Contexts lean toward biographical and record-keeping text: birth years, name suffixes, index entries, religious orders, exhibitions, origin statements. Several members are token detectors inside names. Moderate register coherence.

clusters.name: Mixed technical and web fragments
clusters.desc: No coherent theme. Members fire on tweet embeds, code punctuation, CJK in comments, plotting terms, email obfuscation, and chemistry subwords. Several steer toward 'now'. Treat as a mixed bucket.

clusters.name: Mixed technical/code token detectors
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous technical-text units: patent numbers, bill numbers, code paths, ad-tracking strings, storage terms, birth fields. No shared concept; storage/equipment output appears in two members.

clusters.name: Type/style/mode words and code types
clusters.desc: Output views of several coda units promote or suppress 'type', 'style', 'mode', 'model', 'pattern'. Firing leans toward code type annotations, content types, and static typing discussion. Two views roughly agree.

clusters.name: 'Out' particle and phrasal verbs
clusters.desc: Strong output agreement: most coda members promote or suppress 'out'. Firing hits verbs that pair with out or away (turned, make, come, peel, fall, withdraw) and emphatic idioms. A phrasal-particle family.

clusters.name: Film, TV, and entertainment media
clusters.desc: Contexts are reviews, filmography lists, celebrity news, adaptations, and character discussion. Coda outputs include editor/reporter, character, moment. A meta layer: text about stories and their characters.

clusters.name: Layer-1 STEM and math notation
clusters.desc: Concentrated in one early depth bin; exemplars fire inside scientific papers, LaTeX math, statistics code, and physics jargon. A register of technical/academic STEM text carried by firing.

clusters.name: Concessive connectives: however, though
clusters.desc: Output views of many core-pass-2 and coda members promote or suppress 'however', 'though', 'although', 'yet'. Firing includes concessive or additive discourse markers in some members; others fire on numeric noise.

clusters.name: Patent and engineering descriptions
clusters.desc: Concentrated in one depth bin. Contexts are patent claims and device specifications: reference numerals, figures, components, desired results. Outputs include depicted/shown/arrow, reference/num, cover, project.

clusters.name: 'Down' particle and phrasal verbs
clusters.desc: Many coda members promote or suppress 'down'; firing lands on verbs that pair with down (taken, pulled, turned, die, fall, slow) and on downvote contexts. Mirrors the out-particle cluster.

clusters.name: Base64 blobs; British-spelling output
clusters.desc: Firing in almost every member is inside base64 or encoded random strings. Separately, the Jacobian lens of most members promotes or suppresses British spellings ('whilst', 'utilise', 'characterised'). Two distinct stories.

clusters.name: Mixed old-print and archaic text
clusters.desc: Grab-bag skewed to the coda. Firing contexts lean to scanned older books, verse, bibliographies and dialect speech, but each neuron has its own output story (suppress common/public, band, dark; promote custom). No shared theme.

clusters.name: Repetition: again, once more
clusters.desc: Coherent output family: neurons promote or suppress 'again', 'once', 'repeat', 'anymore'. Firing sits on idioms of recurrence and return (repeating an action, repeated-time idioms, no longer). Pass-1/pass-2 copies of one module both present.

clusters.name: Deixis of place: here and there
clusters.desc: Output family centred on 'here/herein/hither/there': many coda and pass-2 neurons promote or suppress here-words. Firing is on phrases that end in a locative (arriving or being somewhere, operating in this spot). Pass copies 36/933 and 56/933 sit together.

clusters.name: Prelude subword detectors, technical prose
clusters.desc: Large prelude-heavy bin of sharp token or subword detectors in scientific, legal, patent and reference-list text. Jacobian lens often favours British spellings (colour, fibre). Little steering signal; no unifying concept.

clusters.name: The word one: numeral and pronoun
clusters.desc: Output family around 'one/ones/single/none': neurons promote or suppress them; firing on affectionate ones-phrases, a someday opener, and negated or free-choice one. A few outliers (email signatures, articles) ride along.

clusters.name: Difference and variation
clusters.desc: Output family: different/differently/vary/varies/differing promoted or suppressed by core and coda neurons; firing on things that vary by type, something different, another matter. Prelude members are unrelated subword detectors.

clusters.name: Hypothetical and conditional modality
clusters.desc: Neurons around 'would' and counterfactual framing: promoting or suppressing would/might/will, firing in hypothetical clauses, idioms of fate or chance with would, speculative suggestions. One coda neuron about misleading (mis- prefix) and one about God ride along.

clusters.name: Saying and reported speech
clusters.desc: Speech-act cluster: neurons promote or suppress say/said/stated/writing, fire on attribution colons, idioms of saying (suffice it, needless to mention, as they put it), callers and voices introduced as speakers. Meta-language about utterances.

clusters.name: Mathematical and physics exposition
clusters.desc: Genre cluster: firing on equations, LaTeX, definitions, theorems, cosmology and linear-algebra prose, mostly in the coda. Outputs promote or suppress mathy tokens (sum, equation, span/ker, simulation, steady).

clusters.name: Others and remainder, loosely
clusters.desc: Loose bin with a faint output thread: several neurons promote or suppress 'others', 'related', 'ones', 'versions'. Firing contexts are scattered (proof prose, indexes, XML, usenet, Dutch). Mostly pass-2 core.

clusters.name: Religious and devotional writing
clusters.desc: Genre cluster: scripture, hymns, sermons, theology. Prelude-heavy (positions 3-4), Jacobian lens promotes Jesus/heaven/divine/gospel. Firing on biblical diction and devotional abstractions (grace, peace, judgments).

clusters.name: Quantifier all, plus boilerplate
clusters.desc: Loose bin. A thread of neurons promotes or suppresses 'all/everything' (summing-up idioms, all-sizes phrasing, minimizing hedges); another thread is document boilerplate: copyright lines, consent checkboxes, broad-vs-specific patent wording. Many members are foreign-language or code detectors.

clusters.name: Foreign scripts and byte fragments
clusters.desc: Huge prelude-heavy bin of subword detectors for non-English text (Korean, Hungarian, Polish, Estonian, Turkish, Cyrillic), broken UTF-8 byte pieces, URL percent-encoding, base64 and table pipes. Little steering signal; outputs are subword fragments.

clusters.name: Similarity and sameness
clusters.desc: Coherent output family: same, similar, similarly, likewise, identical, resembling promoted or suppressed. Firing on also/too/likewise, simultaneity idioms, resemblance verbs, and unchanged-outcome reports.

clusters.name: Size, scale and magnitude
clusters.desc: Measurement-dimension cluster: outputs promote or suppress size, scale, level, length, total, range; firing on dimension nouns (quality, complexity, length, quantity, step size) and on degree adverbs of change.

clusters.name: Source code: constructors and types
clusters.desc: Code-genre cluster: firing in Go/Java/Dart/C/Python source on constructors, error wrapping, type declarations, function-pointer syntax, method calls; several neurons key on the token new or create. Output views are weak, except a coda neuron for flags and colours.

clusters.name: Particle off and phrasal verbs
clusters.desc: Output family around 'off' (and away/forward): coda neurons promote or suppress off; firing on phrasal verbs such as turned off, went off, took off, put off, carried forward, lights-on/off cycles. Prelude members are unrelated subword detectors.

clusters.name: Continuation and recurrence, weak
clusters.desc: Weak family: Jacobian lens of several pass-2 neurons promotes or suppresses again, still, continued, same, afterward. Firing is scattered (code, logs, Finnish/CJK, email quote headers, as-stated cross-references). Pass copies 28/1168 and 48/1168 share output weights.

clusters.name: Singleton: underscore in URL slugs
clusters.desc: One-neuron cluster. Fires on the underscore joining words inside URL paths and identifiers; negative pole on LaTeX and Mathematica escape sequences. Steering words (love, favorite) do not match the firing.

clusters.name: Pass-2 entry, glitch-token outputs
clusters.desc: Huge spike at position 39, the first pass-2 layer. Members fire on whitespace, digits and markup in structured data; their Jacobian lens points at rare glitch-like merged tokens. Low-meaning machinery, not a theme.

clusters.name: Spatial position: top, bottom, side
clusters.desc: Coherent spatial-layout family: coda neurons promote or suppress top, bottom, left, upper, side, edge, centre, axis. Firing on on-top-of, extreme-position phrases, figure-panel callouts, axes and coordinates in code.

clusters.name: Large mixed bin, core and coda
clusters.desc: Very large heterogeneous cluster peaking at position 38 and through the coda. Each exemplar has its own token-level output (general/public, store, truth/principle, threshold, dark) with unrelated firing in code, citations, old print. No shared theme.

clusters.name: Relative which and clause links, mixed
clusters.desc: Mixed bin where many members fire on 'which', 'where', 'whom' or clause connectors (relative clauses, expressing-via phrasing), but outputs diverge: execute, exist, close, sample, shade, least. Partial syntactic thread only.

clusters.name: Additive also, too, as well
clusters.desc: Coherent discourse-connective family: outputs promote or suppress also, likewise, too, additionally, moreover, furthermore. Firing on not-only-but-also frames, as-well endings, too in negation (either), and sentence-initial Also/Further. Mostly pass-2 core.

clusters.name: Money, research and institutions
clusters.desc: Institutional-register cluster, mostly coda: outputs suppress domain nouns (survey, funding/revenue, penalty/fine, sale/auction, pay, research/study, farm, living). Firing on legislative, finance, real-estate and academic-disclosure text.

clusters.name: Naming and designation of things
clusters.desc: Contexts where something is given, bears, or is known by a name or word: naming babies, pen names, terms and acronyms. Mid/late core neurons promote or suppress name/naming vocabulary; strongly metalinguistic.

clusters.name: Code, encoded data, subword fragments
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous grab-bag of neurons firing inside base64 blobs, CSS/numeric tables, code identifiers and mid-word fragments, plus a few other/else-alternative detectors. No shared semantic theme.

clusters.name: Contrast and substitution (instead/rather)
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons whose output (especially Jacobian lens) promotes instead/rather, set up by contrastive or corrective contexts: not X but Y, rather-than, X-more-than-Y. Firing tokens vary; the output view carries the theme.

clusters.name: Phrasal-verb heads predicting out
clusters.desc: Mostly pass-2 core and coda neurons that fire on verbs taking a particle (find, check, reach, figure, start, work) and promote out/off/into. Several stragglers (waiting/duration, mixed web text) dilute it.

clusters.name: Coda neurons in technical text
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons firing in patents, scientific and code text, many with weak firing selectivity (often on 'are') and word-family outputs. Shared register is technical prose; individual neurons are mostly output-side word-family promoters.

clusters.name: Completed state and prior existence
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to already-ness: steering repeatedly yields already/finished/prepared, outputs promote already, previously, existing. Firing is scattered (Italian gia, sign-up prompts, done deeds), so steering plus output carry the cluster.

clusters.name: Early subword fragments, British-spelling outputs
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude and pass-1 neurons firing on mid-name or mid-word fragments, dialect spellings and non-English text. A recurring output thread: Jacobian lens promotes British spellings (recognise, realise, colour). Otherwise no shared meaning.

clusters.name: Software, computing and systems
clusters.desc: Neurons around software and computing: programming, open source, editors, servers, digital systems. Several outputs promote software/computer/system vocabulary. A sizeable fraction of exemplars are off-topic token or fragment neurons.

clusters.name: Court opinions and legal reasoning
clusters.desc: Firing contexts are overwhelmingly appellate and trial-court opinions: evidence, burdens, admissibility, factors weighed, errors on appeal. Outputs partly agree (evidence/prove/factor, courtroom vocabulary); steering is legal for several.

clusters.name: State, government and jurisdiction
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy neurons about states, national government and jurisdictions in legal/policy text: preemption, state interests, congressional statements. Outputs promote state/federal/nation/foreign; firing contexts are legal and governmental.

clusters.name: Scholarly papers and citation apparatus
clusters.desc: Firing sits in scientific papers, patents and their apparatus: citation strings, journal volume numbers, figure references, author-et-al lists, abstracts. Outputs are mixed; a recurring jlens thread promotes recent-era words (covid, reddit). Firing carries it.

clusters.name: Small counts and enumeration
clusters.desc: Neurons around small cardinal numbers: slots before a count, counted pairs and trios, enumerated lists, statistical df counts. Coda outputs promote two/three/four/multiple; firing is on number words or the space before digits.

clusters.name: Negation and nothingness predictors
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core neurons whose outputs promote negative-polarity words (nothing, nobody, neither, nowhere, didn't, cannot), firing at points where a denial or limitation comes next. Output is the strong view; firing contexts are diverse.

clusters.name: Clause linking around that
clusters.desc: Loose grouping of neurons firing on 'that' as complementizer or relativizer and at inferential clause joints (realization clauses, relatives after issue nouns, no-surprise inferences). Outputs mostly unrelated; a few strong standalone concept neurons ride along.

clusters.name: Comparison between groups (between/among)
clusters.desc: One module seen in both core passes (34/1434 and 54/1434): fires where variation or difference across groups is stated and promotes between/among/amongst. Pass 2 adds steering toward between.

clusters.name: CJK byte fragments in early layers
clusters.desc: Prelude neurons that fire on partial UTF-8 byte tokens inside Chinese/Japanese text (chat logs with numeric IDs, classical prose, code comments). Many are near-pure byte detectors; outputs are noise. A firing-only, formatting/encoding cluster.

clusters.name: Distributive quantifiers (each/every)
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons around distributive and universal quantification: each, every, respectively, per-item tallies, recurring events. Steering often yields each/every; several outputs promote each/respectively. Some exemplars are off-theme.

clusters.name: Persistence and concession (still/yet)
clusters.desc: Neurons for continuation and concessive contrast: outputs and steering converge on still, yet, nevertheless, remain, pending; firing sits at the conjunction or slot before a persisting state or a despite-clause.

clusters.name: Perl module namespace separator
clusters.desc: Singleton prelude neuron that fires on the double-colon separator in Perl module imports; negative pole on fragments of casino/resort names. Outputs uninformative.

clusters.name: The per token and rates
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons whose outputs promote per (and per-prefixed words); steering often degenerates into repeated per. Firing sits before rate expressions (concentration units, sequential handling, following directions). Remaining exemplars are fragment detectors.

clusters.name: Lab methods prose and with
clusters.desc: Firing contexts are dominated by biomedical and chemistry methods sections (buffers, dilutions, staining, quantification, figure callouts), with 'with' a frequent firing token. Outputs are per-neuron word families unrelated to the genre.

clusters.name: Unclear singleton, British-spelling output
clusters.desc: Singleton pass-2 neuron with weak steering and incoherent firing (game item names, numbers in tables and markup). Its Jacobian-lens output promotes British spellings (recognised, whilst, coloured, labelled), the only clear signal.

clusters.name: Early subword and name-piece detectors
clusters.desc: Large mixed bag dominated by prelude neurons detecting word or name fragments (onomatopoeic smack/bam, surname prefixes, initials, city name pieces). Steering is mostly null and outputs are noise; no shared theme beyond token-piece detection.

clusters.name: Size, length and measurement in code
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to magnitude and measurement, mostly in code and markup: sizeof, buffer length/offset arguments, size/orientation properties, numeric types. Several outputs promote size/length/amount/measurement; the rest are code-syntax detectors.

clusters.name: Steering toward URLs and references
clusters.desc: Pushing these pass-2 neurons makes the model emit URL fragments (https, www, com, reddit). Firing touches reference apparatus: footnote numbers after sentences, citation lists, related links, cross-references. Output view is mostly unrelated.

clusters.name: Possessive determiners, mixed outputs
clusters.desc: Firing mostly on possessive pronouns (his, her, your, their, our) in varied prose and dialogue; output views scatter across unrelated families (opportunity/blessing, heart, account, presence). Shared trait is the possessive slot, not a topic.

clusters.name: Present-time output, scattered firing
clusters.desc: Large heterogeneous cluster. Several exemplars write or suppress present-time words (today, current, now, modern) at the readout, but firing contexts range over code, legal text, Spanish, markup and patents with no shared theme.

clusters.name: Video game release description
clusters.desc: Single neuron firing at the sentence end of encyclopedic descriptions of games and media works; output and steering promote released, written, developed, published. All views agree on a who-made-it, when-released register.

clusters.name: Consequence connectives in technical prose
clusters.desc: Output views promote or suppress thus/therefore/hence/consequently; firing sits in technical, scientific, patent and legal expository text (including French and Dutch math). A logical-consequence discourse marker family.

clusters.name: Court opinions and legal documents
clusters.desc: Firing in judicial opinions, case citations, statutes and Federal Register text: citation spacing, enumerated subsections, end-of-opinion boundaries, testimony in hearings. Contains pass-1/pass-2 copies of two modules. Outputs weak; steering mostly absent.

clusters.name: Conversational first and second person
clusters.desc: Firing on I/you and question frames in live exchanges: dialogue scripts, forum posts asking others, service-counter offers, thanks and apologies. Steering leans to please, thank, yes. Speaker addressing a present Other.

clusters.name: Structured-text punctuation, low signal
clusters.desc: Single prelude neuron firing on spacing and punctuation inside citations, escaped JSON and placeholder markup. No steering; outputs incoherent. A formatting position detector.

clusters.name: Biomedical and chemistry paper text
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons firing on subword pieces of scientific terms in biomedical, chemistry and materials writing (tumours in mice, lipids, polymers, bonds, citation numbers). Jacobian outputs sometimes biomedical; steering nearly absent.

clusters.name: Physical environment: weather, terrain, hazards
clusters.desc: Coda and core neurons whose outputs promote concrete physical-world families: mountains, weather and rain, clouds, fire and spills, pain, roads; steering writes wind, sky, scent. Firing is looser, partly on place names and index entries.

clusters.name: Scattered tokens; casual-word Jacobian axis
clusters.desc: Very large, incoherent cluster: firing on fragments in technical, legal, patent and forum text with no shared theme. A recurring Jacobian-lens trait is promoting or suppressing casual vague words (stuff, things, folks, pretty).

clusters.name: Money, prices and markets
clusters.desc: Finance and economics: prices, costs, savings, income, supply, currency, stock indices rising or falling, buyers and sellers. Coda outputs promote cost/price/buyer/currency; steering writes buy, market, revenue; firing in financial news and reports.

clusters.name: Code and machine-text subword fragments
clusters.desc: Large prelude-heavy cluster firing on pieces inside code, SQL, CSV rows, markup, identifiers and non-Latin byte fragments. Steering mostly absent; Jacobian outputs oddly often include British colour spellings. A formatting/fragment detector group.

clusters.name: Additive adverb also
clusters.desc: Single neuron firing on also and then at clause continuations, with likewise, still, even on the negative pole. Firing alone carries it; outputs and steering are weak.

clusters.name: Restrictive quantifiers only/all/any
clusters.desc: Output views (mostly Jacobian) push or suppress quantifier and restrictor words: only, all, any, every, both. Firing contexts are scattered (numbered questions, signatures, numeric strings), so the output trait carries the cluster.

clusters.name: Particle out at the readout
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy cluster whose outputs push or suppress out and outcome tokens; firing is scattered across code identifiers, legal records and citations. Two coda neurons steer into degenerate repeated-letter strings.

clusters.name: OCR'd old printed books
clusters.desc: Prelude and early-core neurons firing on subword pieces in digitized historical print: OCR errors, line-break hyphens, archaic spellings, scripture citations, Latin titles, nineteenth-century sermons and histories. Firing carries it; outputs scatter.

clusters.name: Molecular biology research papers
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons firing on terms in cell and molecular biology papers: knockdown, glucose, luciferase, phosphorylation, genes, bacterial operons, assay protocols. A few outputs agree (bacteria, cluster, protocol); steering nearly absent.

clusters.name: Suffix -able/-ible and ability
clusters.desc: Firing on -able/-ible pieces and the be-able-to construction; coda outputs promote able, ability, ably. Several members drift elsewhere (promise, pain versus worth, formidable), and two coda neurons steer into degenerate repeated suffixes.

clusters.name: Source code syntax positions
clusters.desc: Firing at structural positions in source code across many languages: closing braces, comparison and assignment operators, null-coalescing, conditionals, call sites. Coda outputs on true/false agree; steering mostly incoherent.

clusters.name: Fragments with British-spelling Jacobian output
clusters.desc: Prelude-heavy, incoherent firing (markup, LaTeX escapes, CJK byte pieces, table pipes). The recurring trait is a Jacobian-lens push or pull on British -isation spellings (organisation, organised). Treat as mixed.

clusters.name: United States steering, scattered firing
clusters.desc: The shared trait is steering: many members push generations toward states, united, America, history. Firing contexts are unrelated (French and Spanish legal text, anatomy, plus-minus signs, list numerals); one coda neuron promotes states/countries.

clusters.name: Together, combined, assembled
clusters.desc: Coda outputs push or suppress together, combined, collectively, along; mid-core members write assembling and helping-to-make verbs (put together, thrown together, help to). Firing is looser, often commas joining listed parties or names.

clusters.name: Age, youth and life stage
clusters.desc: Outputs and steering center on age: age/aged/ages, adult, younger, aging, gradually, puberty. Firing includes minimum-age clauses, youth in old biographies, named historical or technological eras, and age-group statistics.

clusters.name: British-spelling Jacobian axis
clusters.desc: Firing is scattered (transcripts, forum replies, names, need/barely contrasts), but many members push or pull British spellings through the Jacobian lens (whilst, utilise, realised, civilisation). An output trait, not a topic.

clusters.name: Auxiliary have/has/had
clusters.desc: Many coda and late-core neurons write or suppress the auxiliary have/has/had/been; firing often lands on have/has. A few members split off to semantic pairs (prevent/inhibition, fun vs trouble, reason, short vs long-term).

clusters.name: Set / collection-noun readout
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons whose output promotes or suppresses the word set (and pair, group, series); firing often lands on the token just before a set-type noun, e.g. data or level preceding it.

clusters.name: Novelty: the word new
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to new / newly: output promotes or suppresses new, firing sits on or next to new in contexts like seasons, fiscal years, new buildings. Some members are loose (culture, continuity).

clusters.name: Mixed: scripture, names, scene
clusters.desc: Grab-bag. A few neurons fire in biblical citation text, some on personal first names, and two late neurons read out the word scene (crime scene). No unifying theme.

clusters.name: Late subword-completion readouts
clusters.desc: Coda neurons each tied to one specific word or stem (sal, flex, rem, con-struction, des-ire, reduction, vertical, Washington): output promotes or suppresses that stem, firing on the token just before it. Lexical, not thematic.

clusters.name: Early multilingual subword noise
clusters.desc: Early-layer neurons firing on subword fragments in non-English text, OCR debris, citation numbers and code identifiers. Several share a lens_down quirk on British spellings (defence, armour). Little steering signal.

clusters.name: Christian scripture and devotion
clusters.desc: Firing contexts are Bible verses, psalms, hymns, prayers and sermons; steering yields lord, god, grace, spirit; output touches prayer, faith, psalm. A coherent religious register across prelude to coda.

clusters.name: Pronoun subjects of mental-state clauses
clusters.desc: Fires on second- and third-person pronouns acting as subject inside embedded clauses about knowing, wanting, believing, doing; outputs read out do/did, mean, desire, believe. Speaker- and addressee-centred clause syntax.

clusters.name: Mixed: possessive its readouts
clusters.desc: Incoherent cluster: chemical name fragments, math notation, Spanish accents, ellipses, code. Several mid and late neurons share an output that suppresses its / itself, but firing does not agree.

clusters.name: Negation and hedged understatement
clusters.desc: Fires on negators in litotes and hedges (denying surprise, harmlessness, softened badness, weaker comparison); outputs read out dont, nearly/half, hurt, bad. Evaluative negation in conversational prose.

clusters.name: Between: relations and intervals
clusters.desc: Strong lexical cluster: output promotes or suppresses between (also among, intermediate, middle); firing on in-between spans, pairs, distances, relationships, alternating and oscillating verbs, values within a range.

clusters.name: Court opinions and legal procedure
clusters.desc: Appellate and trial court register: appellant/appellee, trial court, jury, record, evidence, appeal, review standards. Firing, output and steering all point at judicial prose.

clusters.name: Affect and character traits, loose
clusters.desc: Mostly older narrative prose with emotion or demeanour words: shocking, frightening, relief, pride, disgust, standing tall, bowing. Output links to anger, arrogance, jealousy in places. Loose; several outliers.

clusters.name: Mixed: evaluation and effort
clusters.desc: No clear theme. Members touch caution, effort/attempt, success/fare, quality judgments, problem framing, and dating spam. Each neuron is coherent alone but the group is not.

clusters.name: Figures, tables, cross-references
clusters.desc: Scholarly and patent apparatus: references to figures, tables, sections, citations closing; output promotes or suppresses figure/fig/table/shown. Text pointing elsewhere within its own document.

clusters.name: Singleton: surname fragment
clusters.desc: Single early neuron firing on a subword inside one medical eponym surname; negative pole on very. Output lens unrelated (prayer, violence). Probably a token detector.

clusters.name: Like: similarity and comparison
clusters.desc: Comparison and resemblance: like as preposition, such as, akin, reminiscent, looks/acts like, would like. Output promotes or suppresses like/such; firing sits on the comparison marker or the noun compared.

clusters.name: Singleton: mixed nouns
clusters.desc: Single mid-prelude neuron firing on abstract nouns (elements, nature) and developed; output suppresses philosophy words. No clear story.

clusters.name: From: source, origin, separation
clusters.desc: Preposition from and its semantic frame: derived from, taken from, harvesting sources, distance and removal, exhaustive spans, idioms of continued growth, caused by. Output strongly promotes or suppresses from.

clusters.name: Before / prior / previously
clusters.desc: Temporal precedence: output promotes or suppresses before, prior, previous, beforehand; firing on current-vs-earlier study contrasts, back-references to earlier methods, prerequisites. Includes scholarly back-reference.

clusters.name: Mixed: titles, roles, misc
clusters.desc: Incoherent mixture: subtitle colons, sentence-end punctuation in transcripts, person roles (former, singer, star), activity, normal, stock readouts, honorifics. No shared theme.

clusters.name: Code identifiers and numerics, early
clusters.desc: Early-to-mid neurons firing inside code, markup, URLs, legal citation numbers and Q&A tag lines. Odd shared output quirk: many suppress recent-era topic tokens (pandemic, social apps).

clusters.name: Sports reporting
clusters.desc: Game recaps and sports news: teams, scoring, winning, rivals, leagues, players, natives of places. Output promotes or suppresses football, victory, rival, players. Clear genre cluster.

clusters.name: Ordinals and enumeration
clusters.desc: Ordinal and counting tokens: second, third, fourth, half, numbered list markers and digits inside numbers. Output promotes or suppresses ordinal words.

clusters.name: Back: return and restoration
clusters.desc: The word back and its frame: come back, give back, build back, returning to normality, comeback, missing someone; output promotes or suppresses back/backward/restored. Some outliers (hidden, unwritten, patents).

clusters.name: Mixed: own, ownership, misc
clusters.desc: Incoherent. A few late neurons read out own/owner/opposite/fixed; the rest are early subword detectors in URLs, acronyms and non-English text. No shared firing theme.

clusters.name: Non-English Germanic subword continuations
clusters.desc: Fires inside words of German, Scandinavian, Dutch and other European-language text (inflectional endings, compound joints, old Fraktur OCR). Steering is weak and unrelated; a few coda neurons push nationality or language tokens.

clusters.name: Pass-2 manner and with-phrases
clusters.desc: Mostly core pass-2 neurons firing mid-clause in English prose on prepositions and light verbs introducing manner, accompaniment or circumstance (with, by degrees, playing around). Output lenses and steering point in different directions per neuron; loose overall.

clusters.name: Legal register and purposive 'for'
clusters.desc: Court opinions, motions, statutes and votes, plus the purposive or benefactive use of for (favoring, purpose clauses, lacking). Lenses often promote for/against/favor or complaint vocabulary; steering is weak.

clusters.name: Code, markup and numeric data
clusters.desc: Fires on punctuation, identifiers and digits inside source code, XML/SVG markup, LaTeX, CSV and number dumps. Lenses and steering are noise; a firing-only document-type detector spread over prelude and core pass 1.

clusters.name: Freedom / free-of concept
clusters.desc: Output and steering converge on free, freedom, liberty, clear, admission-free and parameter-free senses; firing is scattered (compounds ending in -free, freeing up, steering clear, free online offers). Mostly coda and core pass 2.

clusters.name: Time, duration and timing
clusters.desc: Output lenses repeatedly promote or suppress time, times, duration and timeframe; firing sits in technical, code and statistics text (time limits, runtime, turnaround, group-by-time interactions). Some members are generic code-punctuation detectors.

clusters.name: Negation and stance verbs
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy group firing around not, never and other negators in prose and legal reasoning; outputs pick out evaluation or stance words (agree, claim, notice, bad, affect, mean). A meta-flavoured layer on asserting, judging and disagreeing.

clusters.name: Elapsed time and temporal spans
clusters.desc: Fires on year numbers, durations and spans (years afterward, decades back, half-century spans); outputs promote or suppress year, month, ago, since, generation and century. Steering also leans temporal. Core pass 2 and coda.

clusters.name: Causal connectives: because, due to
clusters.desc: Output lenses across core pass 2 and coda promote or suppress because, due, since and owing; firing lands on the noun or clause just before a stated reason. A causal-explanation discourse group, with a few code-format stragglers.

clusters.name: Copula before predicate participle
clusters.desc: Fires on is/are/was/were and similar auxiliaries heading passive or predicate constructions; outputs promote the participle that follows (concerned, followed, considered, created, built, obtained) or toggle singular versus plural verb agreement.

clusters.name: Another, other, yet another
clusters.desc: Additive and alternative reference: outputs promote or suppress another, other, yet, something, someone, additional; firing on yet-another constructions, one-another reciprocals and listing of further items. Coda and core pass 2.

clusters.name: Not-so comparative degree
clusters.desc: Single prelude neuron firing on so in not-so-X comparisons in older prose; negative pole on that after reporting verbs in health-claim text. Lenses weak; steering barely relevant.

clusters.name: Mixed: subwords, code, single-concept coda
clusters.desc: No shared theme. Prelude members fire on foreign-language word pieces, dictionary indices or code; coda members each own one output concept (fix, card, character, introduction, sales). Negative pole often lands on the conjunction and.

clusters.name: First, initially, outset
clusters.desc: Order and precedence: firing on first, outset, beginning idioms, first-place and first-step phrasing; outputs promote or suppress first, initially, priority, precedence. Clean core pass-2 concept with some coda support.

clusters.name: Possessive determiners and ownership
clusters.desc: Fires on its, their, his, your, our as possessive determiners and on idioms built around them (owning, credit, duty, peak form). Steering and lenses push possessives or kinship nouns; core pass 2 plus coda.

clusters.name: Onset: begin and start
clusters.desc: Inception verbs. Steering writes began/started, lenses promote or suppress begin/start/beginning, and firing sits on subjects or verbs just before an onset (founding ventures, rising tolls, initial states). Almost entirely coda.

clusters.name: Restriction: only, just, merely
clusters.desc: Exclusivity and limitation. Lenses promote or suppress only, solely, merely, just, single, alone; firing includes not-just contrasts, only-after/not-until timing, in-isolation phrasing. Several members are comma or document-break detectors with an only-flavoured output.

clusters.name: Reflexive pronouns (itself, themselves)
clusters.desc: Output lenses in core pass 2 and coda promote reflexives (itself, themselves, yourself, oneself) and steering writes them; firing is weaker and mixed, including copulas in definitional math prose, try-it-for-yourself web text and stretches of Haskell or C code.

clusters.name: Baby-boomer word piece
clusters.desc: Single prelude neuron completing the boomer word piece after a split stem; negative pole on renouncing. Lenses and steering are uninformative.

clusters.name: Mixed: code subwords, coda one-offs
clusters.desc: No common theme. Early members fire inside code, markup, CJK bytes or Latin filler; negative poles often on -ing pieces. Coda members each carry one output word (link, energy/vibes, throw/try/catch, works).

clusters.name: Only/solely, technical and code text
clusters.desc: Mostly coda and core pass-2 neurons whose output promotes or suppresses only, solely, exclusively, exactly, limited. Firing is scattered across software docs, patents and markup (read-only flags, exemplifying phrases, restrictions). Sibling of the restriction cluster but more technical.

clusters.name: Both, two, pairs and duality
clusters.desc: Quantification over pairs: firing on both, either, neither, two groups, and number pairs; outputs promote or suppress both, neither, two, duo, combined, respectively. Mostly core pass 2 with coda echo; steering often writes both.

clusters.name: Casual-versus-formal register axis
clusters.desc: Shared signal sits in the Jacobian lens: members promote casual words (kids, guys, folks, cute) and suppress formal, historical or legalistic ones, or the reverse. Firing is scattered over older prose, names and OCR; steering unrelated.

clusters.name: Later, subsequently, next
clusters.desc: Temporal sequence after a reference point: lenses promote or suppress later, afterwards, subsequently, thereafter, next, further, eventually; firing on hereinafter, forward references, follow-up, and future-tense will. Coda-heavy with core pass-2 support.

clusters.name: Programming Q&A and source code
clusters.desc: Prelude-heavy group firing in developer forum questions (requests for suggestions, broken-code complaints, pulling data) and inside code (Go, Ada, Fortran, Python, build files). An odd shared lens: many promote British spellings (programme, colour, favourite).

clusters.name: Sufficiency / 'enough' output direction
clusters.desc: Mostly pass-2 core and coda neurons whose output promotes or suppresses enough/sufficient/adequate. Firing is varied: want/need objects, degree words, days of the week; the shared thread is the readout, not the contexts.

clusters.name: Directional particles in phrasal idioms
clusters.desc: Neurons firing on the particle or noun completing motion and result idioms: flooding in, smashed to bits, declining a chance, clothing, total commitment, moving through by some manner. Output often promotes into/onto. Several unrelated detectors also sit here.

clusters.name: Mixed: past-tense copula and fragments
clusters.desc: No coherent theme. Several neurons touch the was/were past-tense readout, others fire on subword fragments, citation digits, table separators or foreign text. Contexts span patents, case law, biology methods and reviews.

clusters.name: Mixed abstract-noun detectors (academic/technical)
clusters.desc: Loose grouping of neurons firing on abstract nouns in expository, academic, medical and patent prose: transition, physical, cure, cognition, representation, context. Each neuron is a different word family; the shared feature is the register.

clusters.name: Source and origin: 'from' readout
clusters.desc: Neurons whose output promotes from/sourced/courtesy, firing at origin points: getting news or ideas from somewhere, attribution lines of reposted articles, travel from a place. Some negative poles touch remote/online access and links.

clusters.name: Comparatives: more, less, than
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy group around comparison. Outputs promote or suppress more/less/better/larger; steering pushes toward 'than'; firing sits on comparative adjectives, degree modifiers and make-more-sense frames.

clusters.name: Prelude subword detectors, technical register
clusters.desc: Early-prelude neurons firing on subword pieces and numerals in scientific methods, patents and code (triplicate, phalange, texture, decimal digits, spelled-out counts). Their lenses share a British-spelling direction that looks like an early-layer lens artefact.

clusters.name: Random strings, hashes, ASCII-art filler
clusters.desc: Early-core pass-1 neurons firing inside base64 blobs, hex hashes, keys and ASCII-art runs of repeated letters or dots. Steering and lens readouts are weak and inconsistent; the firing view alone carries the cluster.

clusters.name: Subword pieces inside proper names
clusters.desc: Neurons firing on the middle or final subword of surnames, given names and place names, mostly in citations, court captions and bylines; some on foreign-language words. Lenses are scattered; this is a tokenization-level cluster carried by firing.

clusters.name: Time as a resource and occasion
clusters.desc: Neurons about time: taking an opportunity, spending or wasting time, having no time, punctuality, pausing to savor a moment. Outputs promote or suppress time/times/hours/timing; steering pushes toward pausing, scheduling or spending.

clusters.name: Numeric data dumps, CSV and floats
clusters.desc: Pass-1 core neurons firing on digits inside comma-separated numbers, float columns and scientific notation. Their lenses share a recent-era vocabulary axis (pandemic, social-media and identity terms) that the firing does not reflect.

clusters.name: Materials and device engineering patents
clusters.desc: Prelude-heavy neurons firing on technical nouns in materials, photonics, electrochemistry and device patents: membranes, wafers, waveguides, solar panels, transparent conductors, ceramics. Firing carries it; lenses partly agree (solar, ceramic, laminated).

clusters.name: First-person plural and authorial 'I'
clusters.desc: Many coda and pass-2 neurons whose output promotes or suppresses our/ours/ourselves, plus neurons firing on first-person stance: an author announcing what they will examine, hedged personal opinion, a speaker recounting what a parent said.

clusters.name: Mixed: single-concept output directions
clusters.desc: No shared theme. Each neuron has its own readout word family (provided, preparation/formulation, ranking/order, remote, power, depiction) while firing is diffuse across function words in formal prose. One sub-thread touches captions and disclaimers about images.

clusters.name: Testing: software tests and exams
clusters.desc: Neurons about tests: unit-test code, test cases in programming problems, exam instructions, trying something out to see what happens. Outputs promote or suppress test/tests/testing/check/validation; firing sits in test files and problem statements.

clusters.name: Preposition 'for': purpose and beneficiary
clusters.desc: Mostly pass-2 core neurons whose output promotes or suppresses 'for', firing where 'for' is due next: searching for, known for, suggestions for, a page meant for you, as for a topic. A clean token-family readout.

clusters.name: Object pronouns and referents (them, him)
clusters.desc: Loose group whose outputs promote or suppress them/they/him/ones and similar pro-forms, firing near object pronouns and anaphoric 'one'. Several unrelated detectors (capitalised headings, word fragments, tearing apart) dilute it.

clusters.name: Mixed: reflexive-pronoun lens, noisy firing
clusters.desc: Several neurons share an output axis on reflexive pronouns (myself, ourselves, yourselves) but fire on unrelated material: table markup, list dashes, units like bpm, foreign text, code. No coherent firing theme.

clusters.name: Way, manner and method
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy neurons centred on way/manner/method: best approach, in this manner, by all accounts, parting company, intensifier uses. Output promotes or suppresses way/ways/manner/method; firing sits on the preceding modifier.

clusters.name: Sufficiency idioms around 'enough'
clusters.desc: Second sufficiency group: outputs promote or suppress enough/sufficient/adequate, and firing sits on idioms of adequacy or excess: impatient anticipation, confirmation, being fed up, concessive approval. Overlaps in theme with the other 'enough' cluster.

clusters.name: Who-questions about a person
clusters.desc: Singleton. Fires on the word right after 'who' in identity questions, including an interjection in a parliamentary record asking who someone is. Steering and lens readouts are weak and unrelated.

clusters.name: Large magnitudes: thousands to trillions
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons whose output promotes or suppresses hundreds/thousands/millions/billions and innumerable. Firing sits near large counts, whole-entire quantifiers, and number abbreviations. A few neurons use the same axis oppositely (local vs global scale).

clusters.name: Modal ability: can, could, possible
clusters.desc: Neurons whose output promotes or suppresses can/could/may/capable/possible, firing on modals in academic prose (this paper can, we can readily see), lifelong-memory phrasing and hedged requests. A clear modal-verb family.

clusters.name: Questions, asking and answering
clusters.desc: Neurons about questions as discourse objects: asking, answering, research questions, Q&A interviews with speaker labels, parliamentary questions, Stack Overflow posts. Outputs strongly promote or suppress question/questions/answers; steering pushes toward asking and wondering.

clusters.name: Here/there deixis and document cross-reference
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy neurons around here/there/herein/therein and in-text pointers: forward pointers to later text, infra/supra in legal opinions, patent therewith/therebetween, bracketed alterations inside quotations. Text pointing at other parts of itself.

clusters.name: Right/left: side, politics, correctness
clusters.desc: Loose family around the word right and its relatives: spatial sides, political wings, being correct, entitlement. Several coda neurons predict or suppress right/left; others are unrelated token detectors.

clusters.name: Coordination in technical lists
clusters.desc: Technical and scientific text with paired or enumerated items: respectively-constructions, vice-versa, comma lists, reference numbers. Coda members are mostly word-piece completers (den-, pro-, main-) with little shared meaning.

clusters.name: Function words in older prose
clusters.desc: Grab-bag of mid-network neurons on prepositions, auxiliaries and connectives, often in 19th-century or OCR-noisy prose. Several share a Jacobian-lens pull toward British spellings. No single theme.

clusters.name: Lowercase pronoun i
clusters.desc: Single prelude neuron that fires on lowercase i serving as first-person pronoun in informal writing; negative pole on hyphens joining words in URL slugs and LaTeX braces.

clusters.name: Instead / rather: substitution
clusters.desc: Substitution and alternatives: the slot before instead, rather-than, in-lieu-of, substituting one thing for another. Output lens of several neurons promotes or suppresses instead/rather directly.

clusters.name: Unclear singleton
clusters.desc: Single core neuron with no coherent firing, steering or output story.

clusters.name: Academic paper apparatus
clusters.desc: Scientific-paper scaffolding: the gap before an Introduction or abstract sentence, citation punctuation, reporting verbs, front-matter labels like Keywords. Several share a British-spelling Jacobian lens.

clusters.name: he after slash or break
clusters.desc: Single prelude neuron firing on he when it follows a She/ slash or a broken line split; negative pole on ove word piece.

clusters.name: Mixed with down-steering residue
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous cluster; steering often adds down, but firing ranges over narrowing a problem, posture/orientation, versions, wiki headings and code subwords.

clusters.name: Question words: how, what, whether
clusters.desc: Interrogative and embedded-question structure. Output of many coda/core neurons promotes how/what/why or suppresses whether/how; firing sits at clause boundaries before wh-clauses, question marks, and help-forum queries.

clusters.name: VR letter-pair detector
clusters.desc: Two prelude neurons both firing on the uppercase VR letter pair inside product names and identifiers; negative poles differ (Pe piece, JSON false).

clusters.name: Conjunction and in informal narrative
clusters.desc: Mostly and-linked clauses in casual and narrative prose: chained actions, fixed binomials, idioms. Mixed in are a surprise neuron, a quoting neuron and a tag-question neuron.

clusters.name: Digits in long numeric strings
clusters.desc: Digits deep inside floats, CSV rows, coordinates and SVG path data. Firing is uniform; steering and output vary and disagree.

clusters.name: Time spans and durations
clusters.desc: Durations and time units: number-plus-hours/days, deadlines, seasons and named days, schedules, employment leave. Pass-2 core neurons dominate.

clusters.name: Code and technical help, from
clusters.desc: Programming and technical contexts (regex, SQL, build paths, random seeds, config) with a shared output/fb lean on from. Includes one paper-boilerplate neuron.

clusters.name: Mixed, etc in Jacobian lens
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous neurons (dates, course codes, hex colours, patent parts, escaped slashes) that share mainly a Jacobian lens toward etc. No coherent firing theme.

clusters.name: Scientific methods and analysis
clusters.desc: Academic methods vocabulary: interpretation, named studies and models, mechanics terms, image terms, et al. citations and figure/equation breaks.

clusters.name: The word one
clusters.desc: Uses of one: one-or-more quantification, generic pronoun one in math, one-hand/other-hand contrast, fine fractions. Output often promotes or suppresses one.

clusters.name: Encoding and code fragments
clusters.desc: Subword and fragment detectors across code, URLs, non-Latin bytes and foreign words. One Usenet attribution neuron stands out.

clusters.name: Legal opinions and case citations
clusters.desc: Court opinions and statutes: docket captions, reporter abbreviations, rule and code section numbers, conclusion formulas, legal prepositions. Prelude-heavy.

clusters.name: Lines, borders and drawing style
clusters.desc: Lines and stroke styling across CSS borders, plotting dash styles, line width, biological cell lines. Output of several coda neurons promotes line/lines.

clusters.name: The preposition for
clusters.desc: Neurons whose output promotes or suppresses for, firing on what precedes it: firsts, scheduled events, setting off on journeys, up-for, memo headings, photo credits.

clusters.name: Other, another, otherwise
clusters.desc: Alternatives and additional items: otherwise, other respects, another kind, apart-by-distance, also. Also contains a Slavic-translation neuron and listing-page boilerplate.

clusters.name: Change and transformation
clusters.desc: Change as a concept: undergoing shifts, things that changed, modifications, agents of transformation. Most coda neurons promote or suppress change words; firing lands on nearby subjects or verbs.

clusters.name: Already, previously, prior state
clusters.desc: Prior or existing state: already, previously, existing, otherwise, and as-if-not-enough compounding. Includes a back-reference neuron for earlier statements and a package-deal detector.

clusters.name: Perfect-aspect auxiliaries, late mixed
clusters.desc: Loose late-layer grouping whose firing often involves have/has/been auxiliary constructions and completed-state verbs; individual members drift to unrelated topics (attraction, happening, effort idioms). Only the auxiliary thread recurs.

clusters.name: Power electronics: converters, regulators
clusters.desc: Small coda cluster on circuit and power-supply technical writing: switching converters, voltage regulators, capacitors and inductors. Firing carries it; output of two members leans to wall/regulator vocabulary.

clusters.name: Early subword fragments, no theme
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons firing on word pieces mid-token (letter repeats, name fragments, latter/former pieces). Several share a British-spelling tilt in the Jacobian lens, but contexts share no topic.

clusters.name: Legal case citation numerals
clusters.desc: Neurons firing inside court-case citations: reporter abbreviations, volume and page numbers, years in parentheses, court names. Mostly prelude; a few Jacobian lenses point at judicial vocabulary. Firing is the clear carrier.

clusters.name: Web page apparatus and commerce
clusters.desc: Grouped by web-page furniture: update and publication stamps, help-support appeals, sale availability, reading/consulting advice, vendor pitch. Steering of several members writes about articles, editing, reading. Loose.

clusters.name: Concession, contrast and reluctant compliance
clusters.desc: Core-pass-2 heavy cluster around contrastive and concessive turns: fires on but/yet/still, and several outputs promote being forced, compelled or resigned. A smaller strand on precision and knowing exactly.

clusters.name: Prelude word-piece detectors, mixed
clusters.desc: Large prelude-dominated group of subword detectors: name fragments, letter clusters, multiples, role/position nouns, press conferences. Jacobian lenses of several lean to British spellings. No shared topic.
