clusters.name: Prelude fragments and line-break hyphens
clusters.desc: Prelude subword detectors with no common subject: hyphenated line-break word pieces in scanned books, surname fragments, home/place, same, film-runtime parentheses. Some Jacobian lenses show Jewish surnames or American states.

clusters.name: Early token detectors, heterogeneous
clusters.desc: Big prelude cluster of single-token and byte detectors: internet, tends, be, emoji bytes, email quote markers, dateline underscores, tilde. Contexts span forums, code, news. No coherent theme beyond early lexical detection.

clusters.name: Markup, code and data-table residue
clusters.desc: Mixed cluster firing inside non-prose material: numeric dumps, assembly, LaTeX tables, JSON, addresses, classical references. Jacobian lenses often show utilize-type words. One member is a clean street-address output neuron.

clusters.name: Number, amount and quantity
clusters.desc: Coda and late-core neurons whose steering and logit outputs push number, numbers, amount, total, percentage. Firing on determiners before counted quantities and on quantification phrasing in technical and math text. Strong agreement.

clusters.name: While/whilst thread, otherwise mixed
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous cluster; the one recurring thread is while/whilst: several Jacobian lenses show whilst/amongst (British register) and coda members steer or promote while/whereas. Firing contexts range from code to old letters to legal prose.

clusters.name: Code and markup syntax tokens
clusters.desc: Fires mainly on structural characters in code, HTML, LaTeX and data dumps (closing tags, backslashes, separators). A secondary thread links first/ordinal and configuration words in outputs. Mostly formatting detectors.

clusters.name: Each, per-unit and division into parts
clusters.desc: Distributive quantity: steering and output push each, individually, divided, halves, evenly; firing on per-unit increments, trial counts, arithmetic and array indexing. Includes a pass-1/pass-2 pair of the same core module (positions 32 and 52, neuron 1514).

clusters.name: Future will and modals, loose
clusters.desc: Several late neurons promote will/shall/gonna or fire on modals, so future reference is the main thread; the rest are scattered word-piece and proceed/pro detectors. Weak semantic coherence beyond that.

clusters.name: Code and tech Q&A, self/this
clusters.desc: Fires in programming material and developer Q&A pages: member access on self, code fences, tag lists, answer-by headers, doc comments. Negative poles often land on this/these. Output views are scattered; firing carries it.

clusters.name: His: possession, style, someone's take
clusters.desc: Coda-heavy group where his and possessive constructions recur in firing, steering or output: a person's style, version, interpretation; pre-hyphen history pieces; burdens and survivors. Attribution to some other individual is the loose shared thread.

clusters.name: Plural copula to predicate word
clusters.desc: Late neurons that fire on are/were and push a predicate concept out: common vs rare, relevant, target, repeated, treated, obvious. Steering and logit lens agree per neuron, with firing on the copula slot.

clusters.name: Any: negative polarity, free choice
clusters.desc: Coherent: many neurons promote any/anyone/anything when pushed and fire on licensing contexts: absence of evidence, parenthetical if-any, least/slightest, almost/nearly, even/ever. Strong steering-output agreement.

clusters.name: Where: locative relatives and definitions
clusters.desc: The word where in several roles: relative clause after a place noun, math notation introducing what a symbol denotes, SQL/numpy where, and moments when something happened. Several outputs promote where/wherein/whence. Also one chat user-turn detector.

clusters.name: Lines and borders, loose
clusters.desc: Weak cluster. Recurring thread is line in several senses: spoken lines and one-liners, border lines, online, product lines, verse. Many members are unrelated surname or word-piece detectors. Low coherence.

clusters.name: Prelude fragments, spelling-dialect lens
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous early-layer detectors (sentence-final periods, foreign-language pieces, OCR apostrophes, name fragments). Jacobian lenses split between British spellings and American civic vocabulary, the only shared signal. No topic.

clusters.name: Time spans and calendar units
clusters.desc: Coherent temporal cluster: outputs promote years, months, weeks, days, weekdays; firing on durations, recent-past phrases, ago/since, countdowns to events. Contains a pass-1/pass-2 copy of one core module (positions 27 and 47, neuron 1587).

clusters.name: Experimental methods and lab science
clusters.desc: Fires in methods sections of experimental papers: treatments, doses, test materials, sample preparation, kits, independent-samples statistics. Outputs promote experiment, simulation, hypothetical, item. Firing and output largely agree.

clusters.name: Prelude acronym and digit pieces
clusters.desc: Large early-layer grab bag: pieces inside acronyms and initials, digits in identifiers and binary strings, and/or slashes in patents, sentence-final periods. Detectors with no shared meaning; output views scattered.

clusters.name: Epistemic hedging and stance adverbs
clusters.desc: Neurons around speaker stance on certainty: output promotes likelihood adverbs, steering yields hedged opinion words, firing sits at evaluative asides and parenthetical stance markers. Mostly core pass 2.

clusters.name: Ability modals can and could
clusters.desc: Fires on and around ability/possibility modals; outputs promote or suppress capability, feasibility, tolerance and failure continuations. Mostly core pass 2 and coda.

clusters.name: Low-level noisy text and code tokens
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons firing on mid-token positions in OCR scans, numeric tables, non-Latin scripts, DNA strings, and source code whitespace. Steering signal rare; output lenses incoherent. A grab-bag of surface-form detectors.

clusters.name: Mixed prelude; program/initiative readouts
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons with incoherent firing; a recurring lens thread is British spellings (programme-type) up or down. Two coda neurons are clean promoters of program/plan words in policy and budget text.

clusters.name: Expository clause links around that
clusters.desc: Fires on complementizer/relative that and demonstratives in explanatory and scientific prose; coda members promote specific predicate verbs (stop, eliminate, generate, reason/why) for the clause that follows.

clusters.name: Mixed; recurring new on negative pole
clusters.desc: No coherent theme: code, citations, scientific notation and listings. A weak common thread is the word new among negative-pole firings and lens readouts. Coda members are clean single-word-family promoters.

clusters.name: Parties, consent and responsibility
clusters.desc: Loose grouping around relations between parties: agreeing, deciding who is responsible, granting permission, joining, addressing a court or committee; you is a frequent firing token. Many members are noisy; coda members promote single word families.

clusters.name: Temporal now and state change
clusters.desc: Neurons centred on present-moment and change-of-state framing: promote or suppress now/today/currently, fire on no-longer, already, will and turning-point words. Steering repeatedly yields now. Firing contexts otherwise heterogeneous.

clusters.name: Relative clauses in technical prose
clusters.desc: Fires around relative pronouns (which, that, whose, wherein) and clause-linking prepositions in academic, legal and patent writing; outputs often promote or suppress relativizers and consequence words.

clusters.name: Online dating spam pages
clusters.desc: Strong genre cluster: fires across keyword-stuffed dating-site and personals spam; coda and late core members promote dating/date/online/match vocabulary. Steering sometimes yields meeting and partner words.

clusters.name: Digits inside dense numeric data
clusters.desc: Fires on digits, decimal points and separators deep inside CSV rows, float dumps, coordinate lists and tables. Steering almost absent; a curious shared output quirk is jacobian-lens promotion of British spellings.

clusters.name: Change and alteration
clusters.desc: Clear concept cluster: neurons whose outputs promote or suppress change/changes/shift and increase vocabulary, firing where something is modified, revised, risen or kept unchanged. Steering consistently yields change words.

clusters.name: Temporal subordinators when/while
clusters.desc: Loose cluster where several members promote or suppress temporal conjunctions (when, whenever, while, during, after); firing contexts are heterogeneous technical, legal and narrative prose. Many members weak.

clusters.name: Empirical research methods sections
clusters.desc: Genre cluster: fires in methods, statistics and limitations sections of empirical (often clinical or social-science) papers; outputs promote research, analyses, sciences, intervention, undergo vocabulary. Steering yields data/research words.

clusters.name: Base64 and encoded blobs
clusters.desc: Large cluster grouped by firing: strongest activations fall inside base64 or similar encoded strings, so contexts are near-identical gibberish. Steering and output views vary freely and do not reflect the blob; firing is likely an off-distribution artifact rather than function.

clusters.name: Mixed; formal-register output tilt
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous firing (scientific, legal, dictionary, numeric). A recurring output thread: several members' jacobian lens suppresses casual words (kids, folks, stuff, amazing) and promotes formal or Latinate ones, suggesting a formal-vs-casual register axis.

clusters.name: Code, web markup and URLs
clusters.desc: Fires in source code, config/JSON, markup and networking text; steering on many members produces URL fragments (https, www, com). Output views mostly incoherent apart from a coda URL promoter.

clusters.name: Person nouns: man, men, people
clusters.desc: Weak thread: many members fire on or promote/suppress generic person nouns (man, men, people, persons, human), including the man suffix in occupational words. Contexts otherwise heterogeneous; several prelude members are noise.

clusters.name: Sequencing, numbering and first
clusters.desc: Loose thread on ordering and document enumeration: numbered sections and list items, ordinal first/second, firstly vs lastly. Coda members are clean single-family promoters unrelated to each other (assumption, arrows/figure styling, term).

clusters.name: Industry, trade and manufacturing
clusters.desc: Loose topical cluster around industrial and commercial activity: trades, mills, industrial waste, import/export, commercial bodies, mining and machinery sales pages. Coda members are clean word-family promoters; prelude members mostly token detectors.

clusters.name: Recipes, food and freshness
clusters.desc: Genre/topic cluster: fires in recipes, ingredient lists and food writing (eggs, spices, fruit, beverages); outputs promote freshness, purity, artisanal or filling vocabulary, and steering yields quality and kitchen words.

clusters.name: Gender and women vocabulary
clusters.desc: Output-led cluster: many members promote or suppress women/female/males/gender words; firing contexts are mostly unrelated (code, timestamps, foreign text), with a few firing on she, Mrs, or gender fields. Mostly an output-direction grouping.

clusters.name: Clinical and epidemiological findings
clusters.desc: Genre cluster: fires in medical research prose (case-control designs, prevalence, outcomes, risk and concentration measures, evidence claims). Outputs promote risk, concentration, motivation and prevalence words. Overlaps with the empirical-methods cluster but more clinical.

clusters.name: Steering yields them (plural object)
clusters.desc: Steering-led grouping: nearly every member, when pushed, makes the model over-produce them; one coda and one core member also suppress them/they in the readout. Firing is heterogeneous (foreign languages, technical, legal); otherwise little shared meaning.

clusters.name: Romance-language forum text
clusters.desc: Firing-led cluster: strongest activations inside Italian, Spanish, French and other non-English text, especially Italian newsgroup/forum posts, mostly on mid-word subword pieces. Steering and output views do not share this theme.

clusters.name: Any-family / negative polarity scope
clusters.desc: Late-layer neurons whose output suppresses or promotes any, anything, anyway, least. Firing sits just before polarity-sensitive continuations: doing it regardless, if-any asides, at-all, much-after-negation. Steering pushes repeated any.

clusters.name: Temporal sequencing: before/after
clusters.desc: Output and steering promote before, after, prior, shortly, immediately; firing on anchor nouns or adverbs of a time relation (right before, after class, days after). Pass-1 and pass-2 copies of module 1912 both present.

clusters.name: Natural history and life-science text
clusters.desc: Firing mostly in botany, zoology, ecology and taxonomy prose: plant parts, species ranges, cultivars, nutrients. Output views scattered (garden, tree, human, insect). A domain cluster with weak output coherence.

clusters.name: Mixed early subword fragments
clusters.desc: Large heterogeneous cluster dominated by prelude neurons firing on mid-word subword pieces, whitespace, and non-English script; output and steer views are unrelated noise. No coherent theme.

clusters.name: Copula slot in questions (single)
clusters.desc: Single neuron firing on the verb slot of wh- or inverted questions across English, Norwegian, French and Dutch (is, be, hyphen in inverted French). Output view unrelated.

clusters.name: Biomedical paper register
clusters.desc: Neurons active inside scientific and biomedical articles: citation brackets, acronyms, gene and cell nomenclature, methods sections, journal names. Output views partly match (publication, patent, practice, physiology).

clusters.name: Exemplification markers (such as, like)
clusters.desc: Output strongly promotes such, like, including, namely; firing on the category noun right before an example list (packages, organizations, diseases). Some neurons cover such-in-manner constructions. Coherent.

clusters.name: Era-vocabulary output axis, mixed firing
clusters.desc: Firing is heterogeneous (subword typos, digits, citations, code). The shared signal is in output: many neurons promote or suppress recent-era vocabulary (pandemic, LGBTQ, crypto, politicians' names) versus older or technical words.

clusters.name: Embedded questions: how/what/whether
clusters.desc: Output promotes or suppresses how, what, why, whether; firing near verbs of knowing, wondering and asking, embedded wh-clauses, and the way-something-is construction. Includes asking-for-help openers.

clusters.name: Software / command-line help register
clusters.desc: Firing in programming and sysadmin text: CLI flags, build commands, install reports, OS versions, error-help forum posts. Output partly agrees (command, install, running).

clusters.name: Mixed: subwords and print apparatus
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous. Some neurons track book or print apparatus (preface, printing, schematic figures); others fire on subword pieces, numbers, or code. Output views do not align.

clusters.name: Either/neither and alternatives
clusters.desc: Output view promotes or suppresses either, neither, both, nor, otherwise, else, half. Firing is weak and multilingual (Russian ni-, Finnish -kaan, Italian altro), suggesting cross-lingual negative/alternative particles.

clusters.name: Mixed: age subword and code syntax
clusters.desc: Incoherent group. Several prelude neurons fire on an age substring (Spanish edad, dosage, Mage); others on LaTeX braces, Prolog cut, CSS, logs. Output views scattered.

clusters.name: Academic self-reference: this paper
clusters.desc: Scholarly meta layer: firing on deictic this/the-authors pointing at the document itself, acknowledgements, aim-of-this-study statements, patent self-reference. Output partly agrees (this, subject, gratitude).

clusters.name: Sufficiency: enough / right amount
clusters.desc: Output view centers on enough, sufficient, appropriate; firing near the right amount, hard enough, not having enough. Remaining members are scattered (screen, guide, related).

clusters.name: Contrast: but / however
clusters.desc: Output view repeatedly promotes or suppresses but, however, yet, whereas. Firing is diffuse: forum comment gaps, code, abstract sentence ends before a however-turn, partial-subset hedges.

clusters.name: British vs American spelling axis
clusters.desc: Output view splits British -ise/-our spellings (analysed, realised, organisation) from American place and institution words (US states, NAACP, statewide). Firing is mixed subword and place-name fragments.

clusters.name: Policy funding language (single)
clusters.desc: Single neuron on policy and program-funding prose (direct and indirect benefits, Title IX); bottom on reform and accountability. Output prefers British spellings and suppresses reform/innovation words.

clusters.name: Code: sets, lists, collections
clusters.desc: Firing in source code around collection types and setters (Set, List, setOf, struct, self._ attributes), plus build and plugin config. Output partly agrees (set, setup, target).

clusters.name: Scope limits: any, not limited
clusters.desc: Hedged-scope language in patents and science: non-limitation boilerplate, at-a-given-value phrasing, drawing firm conclusions, hardly/barely. Output often involves any, exact, significant, fixed. Some members are noise.

clusters.name: Scientific coordination and topics
clusters.desc: Scientific-article neurons around coordinated noun phrases (X and Y in titles and section heads), indicators, markers, surveys, computing, resistance. Output views are topic words matching each neuron.

clusters.name: Legal and court-opinion register
clusters.desc: Firing in case law and legal filings: plaintiff/defendant, pleas, affirmed judgments, costs and execution, signatures, reporter citations, holdings. Output views mostly unrelated.

clusters.name: Dates and weekdays
clusters.desc: Output view strongly promotes weekday and month names; firing near dates, timestamps, deadlines and news datelines, including French date fields. Some members carry news-report idiom instead.

clusters.name: Third-person they/them output
clusters.desc: Output promotes they, them, their, there in many late neurons; firing is diffuse (they-learned, they-knew, verbs taking them). Others carry single word families (felt, die, base, logic, learn).

clusters.name: Other / others / else
clusters.desc: Output centers on other, others, another, else, otherwise; firing on among-others phrasing, remainder-of-group phrasing, and alternative or patent or-constructions. Coherent alterity token family.

clusters.name: Coda phrasal-particle predictors (off/away)
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons that fire on a verb or object needing a directional particle and push or suppress the particle itself (off, away, back). Steering adds the particle words. Token-level completion machinery, not a theme.

clusters.name: Code identifiers, keys and name fields
clusters.desc: Neurons firing inside source code, config and tabular headers: attribute names, string types, keys, paths, query parameters, Name columns. Several outputs promote or suppress the word name. Mostly core pass 2.

clusters.name: Science/researchers output axis
clusters.desc: Loose group whose common thread sits in the lens view: many neurons push or suppress words for scientists, researchers, laboratories. Firing is scattered (science journalism, attribution of studies, subword fragments). Some steer toward university-study reporting.

clusters.name: Safety, protection and comfort
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to safety, protection, security and comfort vocabulary: margins of safety, protective measures, safe havens. Strongest in pass-2 core and coda output/steer. Three layer-9 prelude neurons share mirrored lens sets and fire on unrelated tokens.

clusters.name: Romance-language subword fragments
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude and coda neurons firing on word-internal subword pieces in French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese text (verb stems, endings). Outputs are fragment tokens or unrelated; steering is weak. A language/tokenization family, not a meaning.

clusters.name: The word case (instance/scenario)
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons whose output promotes or suppresses case, cases, instance, situation, scenario, and whose steering adds case. Firing covers the slot before case-style nouns (quantifiers, severity adjectives, individualized rulings). Includes a programming CamelCase detector and a hospital neuron.

clusters.name: Exemplification: for example, hypotheticals
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons around giving an example: they fire where an illustration is introduced and their outputs promote or suppress example/examples/scenario; steering adds example. Clear discourse-function family.

clusters.name: Mathematical and technical exposition
clusters.desc: Neurons firing in math, physics and technical writing: definitions, equation references, assumptions, conditions, worked problems. Outputs lean to theory, assumption, optimality, or suppress math words. Register grouping more than one function.

clusters.name: Frequency hedges (sometimes/often/usually)
clusters.desc: Neurons whose output axis promotes or suppresses frequency and generality adverbs (sometimes, often, usually, occasionally); steering adds always/often/sometimes. Firing sits on frequency phrasing, generalizations and concessive openers. Clear hedging/generality family.

clusters.name: Number words and digit streams
clusters.desc: Neurons firing inside digit strings (CSV rows, decimals, SVG path data, citations) whose outputs promote or suppress spelled-out number words (seven, nine, four); steering adds number words. Mostly coda. Numeric token family.

clusters.name: Health advice and wellness copy
clusters.desc: Neurons firing in consumer health and wellness writing: illness, risk, diet, exercise, medication, doctor visits. Outputs push related abstract words (risk, exercise, depend, worse, reduce). A web health-content register; mostly coda and pass-2 core.

clusters.name: Into: division, conversion, categorization
clusters.desc: Neurons around the preposition into and what follows it: dividing into parts, falling into categories, converting or mapping into a form, entering into force. Many fire on or gate into; outputs promote the destination noun (category, mapping, region, conversion).

clusters.name: Data-dump digits; casual-vs-formal lens
clusters.desc: Core neurons firing on digits inside raw numeric dumps, hex, CSV and encoded blobs. Their shared output trait is a casual-vs-formal word axis (stuff, pretty, really, kids vs formal/technical words). Firing is formatting; output carries a register axis.

clusters.name: Second-person address, forum asks, thanks
clusters.desc: Loose pass-2/coda group where firing often lands on you and on forum or advice exchanges (asking for help, thanking, raising a point or concern). Outputs are varied single words (thanks, concerns, approach, desire). Weakly about addressing an Other.

clusters.name: Colloquial vague words (stuff/things/guys)
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons whose output axis is colloquial vague vocabulary (stuff, things, guys, pretty, weird) against formal or elevated words. Firing is mixed: spoken-style asides, dialect speech, mild oaths, kind-of hedges. Register carried mainly by the output view.

clusters.name: British-spelling lens axis (whilst/utilise)
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude and pass-1 core neurons sharing one output trait: their Jacobian lens promotes or suppresses British-style formal words (whilst, utilised, amongst, behaviours). Firing is heterogeneous token-level and steering weak, so the grouping is an output-direction artifact.

clusters.name: Mixed: code tokens, that, Q&A comments
clusters.desc: No single theme. Many neurons list that among firing tokens; firing spans code signatures, encoded strings, numbered identifiers, and Q&A comment threads. A few coda neurons cleanly promote one word (benefit, package, matter).

clusters.name: Fiction scene action and gesture beats
clusters.desc: Neurons firing in narrative fiction on character movement and body language around dialogue: turning round, glancing, holding, standing, character pronouns, addressing a spouse or guests. Steering adds character and scene words. Strong narration-and-speech signal.

clusters.name: Into: motion, entry and transition
clusters.desc: Neurons around into/onto as motion or state-entry (movement, contest entry, fashion trends, compliance, collapse). Several promote or gate into; others promote the landing noun (compliance, prize, fashion, memory). Overlaps the other into cluster.

clusters.name: Negation slot (not) and its neighbors
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons whose firing touches not and the words around negation: not-obvious claims, may-not, choice-left-to-reader, null checks, multilingual negators. Outputs are scattered single words (hard, sit, stop, super, negated auxiliaries).

clusters.name: Math/science notation; British-spelling lens
clusters.desc: Early-layer neurons firing in technical and mathematical prose: variable symbols, products and crosses, i.e./e.g. abbreviations, non-zero, respectively. Outputs share the British-formal axis (whilst, utilised). Firing is register-level; output axis is the same artifact as cluster 340.

clusters.name: Code syntax and markup tokens
clusters.desc: Neurons firing on syntax inside source code, LaTeX, HTML tables and notebook JSON: comment markers, escapes, rowspan attributes, case/default blocks, inline backticks. Some coda outputs promote a programming word (expression, default, operation). Formatting family.

clusters.name: End/ending token family; mid-word fragments
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons where end, ends, ended or -end- subword pieces recur in the output lens or the firing lists (medical compounds, final position, weekend). The rest fire on mid-word fragments in all-caps or OCR text. Token family, little meaning.

clusters.name: You in direct speech and confrontation
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons whose firing centers on you as an addressee in spoken exchanges: confrontations, questions to someone, telling someone something, insults. Outputs vary: profanity, favour/honour, preference, talking words. One neuron is about spelling and pronunciation.

clusters.name: URLs, links and web references
clusters.desc: Neurons that anticipate or follow web links: the slot before a URL, link/refer/see-also wording, site credits and theme footers, platform names. Outputs and steering push http/https/www, website, wikipedia. Strong three-view agreement; reference apparatus of web text.

clusters.name: Gerund and progressive aspect (being/having)
clusters.desc: Neurons tied to ongoing-process and -ing forms. Coda neurons promote or suppress being/having at the readout; steering yields being; firing sits on progressive verbs and rate-of-change phrasing. Many pass-2 core members.

clusters.name: Technical/code text, mixed tokens
clusters.desc: Grab-bag of neurons firing in patents, code, scientific papers and encoded strings, plus several coda neurons whose output promotes for or single word families (cycle, coordinate). No shared semantic theme.

clusters.name: British spelling, academic/scientific prose
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons firing in scientific, medical and institutional writing whose Jacobian-lens outputs consistently involve British/Commonwealth spellings (programme, organisation, colour). Firing tokens themselves are scattered word pieces.

clusters.name: Base64/encoded blobs, number-word outputs
clusters.desc: Fires inside long base64 or random alphanumeric strings and digit runs. Outputs strongly promote or suppress spelled-out number words (five, six, seven, nine). Low steering signal; a formatting detector with a numeric output side.

clusters.name: Government, legislative and civic institutions
clusters.desc: Fires in congressional records, legal filings, press releases, grants and campaign finance. Several coda neurons promote one institutional word family (committee, grant, schedule, contribution). Public-affairs register.

clusters.name: Scientific methods prose, passive was/were
clusters.desc: Fires on was/were and passive auxiliaries in methods and results sections of papers. Coda members each promote or suppress one verb family (completed, removed, created, found, presented, effective). Lab-report register.

clusters.name: Chemical and biomedical word pieces
clusters.desc: Prelude-heavy group firing on sub-word fragments inside chemical names, lab techniques and biomedical terms (prefixes like di-, dim-, chloride, voltammetry, resonance, subscripts in patents). Little steering signal; token-level detectors within technical science text.

clusters.name: Epistemic hedging (probably, perhaps, seems)
clusters.desc: Pass-2 core and coda neurons whose outputs promote or suppress hedging adverbs (probably, possibly, perhaps, presumably, seems). Steering produces hedges for several. Firing is weaker: hedge words, parenthetical asides, forum Q&A.

clusters.name: Coda single-noun-family outputs, formal prose
clusters.desc: Mostly last-layer neurons each promoting or suppressing one content word family (official, decomposition, investigated, secret, green, character, criminal, decision, job). Firings fall on the/noun slots in legal, governmental and academic prose; no shared concept.

clusters.name: Places, regions and geographic scale
clusters.desc: Neurons around place names and geography. Jacobian-lens outputs contrast global scale (countries, nations, Europe, America) against local units (township, parish, county, staff). Firing hits place-name pieces, regions, land and climate descriptions.

clusters.name: Casual colloquial register (pretty, stuff)
clusters.desc: Informal conversational and forum speech: intensifiers and vague nouns (pretty, really, kind of, stuff, folks, guys). Outputs promote or suppress casual words versus formal/academic ones; firing on chatty first-person prose and dialogue.

clusters.name: Knowing, seeing, hearing, remembering
clusters.desc: Cognition and perception verbs. Outputs promote or suppress know/see/hear/aware/recognize/remember and evidential verbs (shows, demonstrates); firing on know/understand/remember in first-person asides, testimony and advice text.

clusters.name: Part/portion word family
clusters.desc: Coda-dominated group whose outputs promote or suppress part, parts, portion, party, particular, and nearby nouns (medium, guide). Firings are on determiners and quantity words just before such nouns. A word-family output cluster.

clusters.name: Possessive pronouns (their, his, its)
clusters.desc: Output-carried: neurons promote or suppress possessive and reflexive pronouns (their, theirs, themselves, his, its, own, personal). Steering often yields their/own. Firing is scattered word pieces, much of it non-English text, with no matching theme.

clusters.name: British whilst spelling, code/markup firings
clusters.desc: Views disagree. The Jacobian lens repeatedly involves whilst, amongst and other British spellings (organisation, utilise); firing sits on code, markup, CSS, forum metadata and odd whitespace. Treat as an output-side British-orthography direction with incidental technical firings.

clusters.name: Relative clauses and which-linkage
clusters.desc: Neurons around relative pronouns and clause linking in expository prose: firing on which, with/via/through before which, and on the noun heading a relative clause; outputs promote or suppress which/whom/whose/wherein. Some coda members carry unrelated word families.

clusters.name: Singleton: code tokens, no theme
clusters.desc: One weakly steered neuron firing on code keywords and technical nouns with scattered outputs. No coherent theme.

clusters.name: Code syntax and you-address, mixed
clusters.desc: Loose group: code punctuation and markup, input prompts asking the user to enter something, Q&A replies addressing you, plus a few single-word coda/core outputs (enter, crazy/insane). Some second-person flavor but no single theme.

clusters.name: Directional prepositions into/onto/from
clusters.desc: Outputs promote or suppress into, onto, from, until and the nouns completing fixed phrases (consideration, mind, space, office). Firing on take/put/into in idiomatic motion and placement phrases.

clusters.name: Biomedical lab research prose
clusters.desc: Firing concentrated in molecular biology and clinical research text (assays, genes, proteins, disease). Coda members each promote or suppress one word family (transport, delete, activity, heart, DNA vs skill, functional, standard, epidemic diseases).

clusters.name: Scanned old books, British colour spelling
clusters.desc: Prelude neurons firing in OCR-scanned historical books and legal reports (page headers, garbled characters, hyphenated compounds, old dialogue). Jacobian-lens outputs repeatedly involve British spellings, especially colour. Archival-print register.

clusters.name: Name word-pieces and her-fragments
clusters.desc: Mostly prelude neurons firing on sub-word pieces inside personal and place names (surname endings, given-name fragments), plus her as a sub-word piece, usually negative pole. A few carry a male-versus-female pronoun axis through the Jacobian lens.

clusters.name: Numeric tables, hex dumps, CSV data
clusters.desc: Fires inside runs of digits: comma-separated values, coordinate lists, timestamps, hex dumps, UUIDs, SVG path numbers and spaced numeric tables. Almost no steering signal and scattered outputs; a formatting/data-blob detector family.

clusters.name: Complementizer that, expository linkage, mixed
clusters.desc: Loose group. Several neurons promote or suppress that (complementizer) and those/these, one fires on forward-pointing signposts in papers and opinions; the rest are coda single-word outputs (lead/trial, clear, scheme, difficult, fulfil/satisfy).

clusters.name: Minimizer adverbs: just, simply, merely
clusters.desc: Clean output cluster: core-pass-2 and coda neurons promote or suppress just, simply, merely, mere, plain, exactly. Steering yields just/simply; firing often on just in casual first-person speech and on intensifiers. Pass-2 core and coda agree.

clusters.name: Temporal anchoring and recency
clusters.desc: Neurons around time reference: whether events are recent, ongoing, habitual or at a dated point. Output views push recency or present-time adverbs (or suppress them); firing sits on time nouns, frequency words and process verbs.

clusters.name: Mixed; late 'head' writers
clusters.desc: Heterogeneous firing across names, archaic verse, foreign text and tables. The recurring thread is in steering/output: several coda neurons push or suppress the word head (and chair, body). Otherwise no shared theme.

clusters.name: Our/we writers plus subword pieces
clusters.desc: Loose grouping. A strong sub-thread of neurons whose output promotes first-person plural possessives (our, ours, ourselves), firing on inclusive-we framing. The rest are subword-completion detectors and a few late suffix writers.

clusters.name: Source code and programming context
clusters.desc: Neurons firing inside source code, config and API documentation: identifiers, type names, operators, JSON and serialization. Output views are mostly unrelated; a few steer toward writing code, scripts or files.

clusters.name: Point/points writers (coda)
clusters.desc: Mostly late coda neurons whose steering and lens output push or suppress the word point(s), firing where a point-like noun is due: viewpoint phrases, weak point, center, critical point, credit points, in-terms-of framing.

clusters.name: Conversational deixis and speaker stance
clusters.desc: Informal, spoken-register text where the speaker points back with that/this, clarifies what they mean, or signals tone (joking, serious, how something sounds). Many firings on demonstrative that in casual speech and dialogue.

clusters.name: Vast-quantity words over technical text
clusters.desc: Firing is on technical and numeric material (digits, ranges, code, citations, tables, patents). The shared signal sits in the Jacobian lens: many neurons promote or suppress huge-magnitude words (millions, billions, trillions, countless).

clusters.name: Code identifiers; odd US-history steering
clusters.desc: Firing is on programming syntax: keywords, property names, refs, constants, type checks, module paths. Output views are unrelated. Curiously several members steer generation toward United States and history words, an off-theme steering artifact.

clusters.name: Trying, testing, and fun
clusters.desc: Loose grouping around attempting and testing (test, try, attempt, testify) plus playfulness and fun. Several late neurons write test/testing; a pass-1/pass-2 pair writes fun and amusement. Remainder are unrelated subword or foreign-text detectors.

clusters.name: Totality: all, everything, whole
clusters.desc: Neurons around universal quantification and wholeness: idioms built on all, the whole of something, everything. Lens outputs promote all/everything/world or suppress them; firing sits near all in fixed expressions.

clusters.name: Through / via writers (coda)
clusters.desc: Mostly coda neurons whose steering and lens output push or suppress through (also thru, via, using), firing where a through-phrase is due: going through hardship, running text through a check, cooked through, passing through.

clusters.name: Statutory and legal-document register
clusters.desc: Neurons firing in statutes, regulations, court opinions and legislative records: section markers, quoting a provision partial-quote, shall-clauses, amendments, definitions. Heavy on cross-reference apparatus. Output views mostly unrelated except a few (relevant, legal, approved).

clusters.name: Second-person address to the reader
clusters.desc: Marketing, advice and help text that speaks to the reader as you: customize your own, if-your-gadget, answering-yes yes. Lens outputs promote (or suppress) your/yourself; firing on the slot just before reader-directed possessives.

clusters.name: Relative clauses and which-constructions
clusters.desc: Syntax neurons around relative and anaphoric linking: which/whom/wherewith, which-case, manner-in-which, from which. Firing concentrates on relativizers and their antecedent nouns, often in older or formal prose; output views mostly unrelated.

clusters.name: Tech/forum text; your-promoting outputs
clusters.desc: Firing is on software, markup and Q&A-forum material (API docs, code, help threads). Several members share a Jacobian-lens push toward your/yours, but firing and steering do not echo it. Largely a technical-register grab bag.

clusters.name: Patent specification register
clusters.desc: Neurons firing in patent and technical-specification prose: component reference numerals, figure references, embodiments, including-but-not-limited-to boilerplate, devices with processors and servers. Several steer toward computing vocabulary; one steers squarely into patent claims language.

clusters.name: There / therein writers (coda)
clusters.desc: Mostly late neurons whose lens output promotes or suppresses there and its archaic compounds (therein, thereof, thereto), firing where existential or locative there is due: is there, there are, limited thereto. Firing contexts themselves are varied.

clusters.name: Source and derivation: from-phrases
clusters.desc: Neurons around provenance and derivation: data comes from, drawn from, gleaned from, from a given perspective, going from one state to another. Lens outputs strongly promote or suppress from; firing on the verb or noun that licenses it.

clusters.name: British vs American spelling axis
clusters.desc: Mostly early-layer neurons whose Jacobian-lens outputs split along spelling dialect: one side promotes British forms (-our, -ise, -re, defence, licence), the other American forms. Firing contexts are heterogeneous single-token detectors, so the dialect signal lives in output.

clusters.name: Code syntax; home-repair steering
clusters.desc: Firing is on code syntax (assignments, imports, stream operators, config files). Output views are unrelated. A notable steering sub-thread: several early neurons push generation toward house repair and renovation (walls, floors, plumbing, kitchens).

clusters.name: Concession and contrast: but/though
clusters.desc: Discourse neurons around concession and contrast: but, though, however, technically, cannot-resist, in a nutshell. Lens outputs push or suppress contrastive connectives; firing sits at the clause junction where a qualification arrives.

clusters.name: Digits inside CSV/timestamp rows
clusters.desc: Firing is on individual digits inside machine-generated tabular data: comma-separated records with timestamps, IDs and counts, and date-time strings. Output and steering views are unrelated and mutually inconsistent; this being a data-format detector cluster.

clusters.name: Spelled-out number words
clusters.desc: Mostly mid/late neurons whose steering and lens outputs push or suppress written-out cardinal numbers (four, five, six, thirty), firing where a count comes next: up to N, one of N, a few, Nth-fifths votes.

clusters.name: Legal and government documents
clusters.desc: Firing concentrates in court opinions, codes, agency memos and congressional records: possessives on party names, cross-referencing see-memo citations, statute names, senators. Late members each write one related word (cause, property, competition, brief); no single output theme.

clusters.name: Text self-reference: here/this/herein
clusters.desc: Document deixis: the text pointing at itself or its venue (this paper, for-this-instance, as follows, herein, this forum or thread). Lens outputs push or suppress here/herein/this; firing on article, findings, forum and posting apparatus.

summary: When neurons are grouped by the meaning of the passages that make them fire, genre and register stand out as a major axis. The earlier, word-based map missed it. Each kind of text (legal, biomedical, patents, math, scripture, old books, web spam, sports) gets its own clusters at every depth. Early layers detect pieces of its terms; late layers pick its words. Genre and register account for 15% of neurons. The function-word and connective families from v0 are still there and are still the clearest (time and discourse are 43% and 37% high agreement). The meaning-based map adds four things the word-based map lacked: a strong narration cluster of 342 neurons (gestures and actions between lines of dialogue), separate clusters for saying and asking, clusters for addressing someone and for confrontation, and a small but coherent layer for text that refers to itself or to other texts (33% high agreement). Archetypes are thin: devotional/scriptural is real, there is one weak affect bin, and no dread, quest, tenderness or trickster cluster. Noise is lower than in v0: lens-only artefacts are 6% (24 clusters, mostly British spelling), unassigned 9%, subword detectors 9%, numeric/encoded 4%. 26 clusters have three neurons or fewer. 15% of neurons are in high-agreement clusters.
